variant_reviews.comparison: The source defines independence of real polynomial functions and then allows any subset of the invariant polynomial algebra. AlgebraicIndependent captures absence of a formal polynomial relation after establishing the polynomial-function interpretation over the infinite field of reals. Algebra.trdeg and IsTranscendenceBasis concern a whole ambient algebra, so they cannot simply be applied to an arbitrary source subset. The inspected algebraic-independence matroid does support bases inside arbitrary subsets of a domain; specialize that construction to the polynomial algebra and relate its restricted rank to the source maximum cardinality. Do not replace the subset by the whole invariant algebra or claim that this comparison has proved the finite-cardinality and evaluation bridges.

The result acts on L2(R); I-star composed with I instead acts on the RKHS and is a different operator. variant_reviews.comparison: The condition applies to the differential of the specified periodic Holder map on torus coordinates and uniformly over the whole cube. Realize the derivative as a Euclidean linear map, with adjoint-composition matching the printed transpose-Gram matrix. The square root of its smallest domain eigenvalue gives the minimum singular value for the d-dimensional domain. Mathlib's singularValues is a natural-indexed finitely supported sequence extended by zero, so taking its infimum over all natural indices would always include artificial zero padding and would not express the source condition; restrict to the genuine d domain indices. Retain the inherited Holder regularity and positive K domain, justify derivative existence rather than use totalized fderiv, and distinguish this immersion/rank bound from global injectivity, manifold regularity or a direct density bound with respect to ambient p-dimensional Lebesgue measure. The formal Theorem 5.1 requires this on g-star only, unlike its overview.

variant_reviews.comparison: Treat the nonnegative random variable with its measurability and measure-specific expectations. Nonnegative integration retains infinity under alternative laws while validity bounds null expectations by one; exactness is equality under every null law, not equality of its full null distribution or pivotality. Expectation nontriviality under each alternative and strictly positive expected log under each alternative are distinct conditions; a positive uniform infimum over alternatives is stronger still. Real.log is the ordinary positive-domain logarithm but defines log 0 as zero, so using it unchanged for a nonnegative e-variable would not supply the usual log-zero minus-infinity convention. The source passage does not spell out extended-log expectations or integrability: retain that qualification, handling zero and positive/negative parts explicitly rather than letting the real integral's zero fallback settle e-power. Do not impose strict X>0 on validity alone.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use Kernel together with IsMarkovKernel, since an unrestricted mathlib Kernel need not have probability-valued fibers. The right kernel R acts first, then Q; Measure.comp_assoc matches Q(RP)=(QR)P and the kernel composition integrates in that same order. Deterministic kernels map x to the Dirac law at the measurable T(x), yielding ordinary measure pushforward, and composition with one evaluates the next kernel at T(x). Apply set image to a statistical model, keeping blackletter laws/kernels and calligraphic models separate. These constructions hold for general measurable spaces with supplied measurable kernels/functions; no StandardBorel condition is needed here. The source phrase linear mapping on probability measures denotes mixture-preserving action, not an assertion that probability measures themselves form a vector space.

variant_reviews.comparison: For positive smoothness theta, the nonnegative spectral multiplier x^theta is continuous on the positive compact operator's spectrum, so CFC.rpow represents the bounded positive power after identifying the source L2 operator with its ordered star algebra instance. variant_reviews.comparison: Specialize the resolvent transform to a Borel probability measure on the real line and complex codomain, giving precisely integral (x-z)^(-1) with no sign reversal. Restrict z to the open upper half-plane; the denominator never vanishes there and the integrand is bounded by 1/Im(z), so probability-measure finiteness supplies integrability even for unbounded support. The negative reciprocal is then -1/m(z), with nonvanishing justified by the strictly positive imaginary part of this transform rather than by total inverse at zero. This construction is generic for original, tilde and Marchenko-Pastur laws, not a particular equation for the last family. StieltjesFunction/CDF is a different object and is not substituted for the complex transform.

variant_reviews.comparison: For a fixed input and output measurable space, require a Markov kernel and the multiplicative probability inequality for every measurable output event and every ordered input pair. This is pure local privacy with no additive delta, no data-adjacency restriction and no almost-sure relaxation over inputs. Swapping inputs supplies the reverse inequality, but no density or Radon-Nikodym version is part of the definition. Kernel values are ENNReal while the coefficient exp(alpha) is a finite positive real, so coercions must preserve those values. The unrestricted union over every measurable output space is a class/universe-level formulation, not an ordinary Set of a single fixed Kernel type. Retain the author's attainable-real-values interpretation for scalar suprema rather than claim one fixed-output formalization covers that union.

variant_reviews.comparison: Keep the iid input-sample premise and a measurable probability kernel for each release using only X_i and the preceding released values. Iterated compProd can build the joint release law while retaining the raw sample as an external parameter, with each component restricted to the allowed current coordinate and history. The allowed history dependence does not make releases independent or imply an alpha privacy bound absent from this passage. A conditional-law assertion alone on almost-everywhere histories is not automatically an everywhere-specified channel.

Keep the joint-kernel factorization for every raw input vector and potentially distinct release spaces. Compose Markov kernels using only x_i and preceding sanitized outputs; an empty history is a singleton empty product, not an empty probability space. Alpha-sequential privacy additionally requires every component channel to satisfy the local inequality at every released history, including histories of zero probability. The generic composition-product and finite-trajectory machinery supply the law but do not prove privacy automatically or permit access to future/raw past inputs.

The central sigma-field is the minimal sufficient sub-sigma-algebra of the covariate information and is generated by f0(X). The inspected conditional-independence predicate can express sufficiency but does not prove existence or uniqueness of a least such field under domination; a lattice infimum alone does not establish sufficiency. variant_reviews.comparison: Keep one joint law P of the full concatenated sample, with each training marginal P0 and test marginal Pi. Equality of probability measures Pi=P0 determines the null index set; it is not a pointwise sample-value comparison or a test decision. The alternative indices are the complement within the m test indices, with counts and proportions using denominator m and the literal offset n+i into the full sample. A positive m is needed for ordinary statistical proportions; natural division must be coerced to real ratios rather than truncated. Training observations need only the common marginal law at this point: independence, conditional exchangeability, no ties and positive densities enter separately later. Pushforwards of coordinate projections or HasLaw express the marginals, while finite predicates and complements give the index sets. No product joint law or iid training sample is inferred from the phrase null training sample.

variant_reviews.comparison: Keep rho squared as one half of triangular discrimination, not squared Hellinger distance. For a concrete dominating measure choose mu=P+Q, which dominates both probability laws, and take real versions of their finite-almost-everywhere RN derivatives a and b; a+b=1 mu-almost everywhere, so the displayed formula becomes half the integral of (a-b)^2 with respect to mu. This representation accounts for mutually singular mass as well as common mass, unlike taking only dP/dQ. For R=(P+Q)/2 and u=dP/dR-1 the equivalent expression is int u^2 dR, subject to establishing those RN identities; no factor four is inserted. Values on simultaneous zero-density null sets need a harmless explicit representative convention. The finite-measure RN and integral APIs express the scalar quantity; the square root supplies rho but does not prove its triangle inequality or the asserted topological equivalence with Hellinger.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each pair P,Q form its own mixture law R and centered positive integral operator T on L2(R), set u=dP/dR-1, and require actual range membership in T^theta with theta>0 plus rho squared>=Delta. For the selected K use that kernel own centered T_K on the pair-specific L2(R), require u in its theta-power range and retain the same rho-squared separation. This is a family of alternative classes indexed by K, not an intersection requiring one pair to satisfy every kernel. Preserve the source theorem use of unsubscripted T in a source-norm hypothesis and disclose the mismatch rather than editing it to T_K. variant_reviews.comparison: This d_Sigma(n) is an admissible envelope at least n, required to bound every inclusive tail sum from l=k through d by d_Sigma*sigma_k for 1<=k<=min(n,d). It is not defined as a minimum, the stable rank trace(Sigma)/norm(Sigma), or a ratio for one chosen k. With d infinite, use the summable nonnegative eigenvalue series supported by the trace assumption, preserving inclusion of k; use finite sums in finite dimension without adding a new source zero-extension convention. The inspected ENNReal conversion requires the total extended sum to be finite, not merely a formally defined tsum. If sigma_k=0 the multiplied inequality requires the nonnegative tail to vanish; dividing by sigma_k loses that case. The envelope can depend on n and need not be asserted integer merely because it is called a rank. Later noninteger, out-of-range and sigma_infinity eigenvalue indices remain separate source limitations.

variant_reviews.comparison: Positive functional-calculus powers can express Sigma^(1/2) for the bounded positive covariance. The second source display requires beta to be in its actual range, with an H-valued finite-norm preimage theta; range closure or finite prediction norm is weaker. If covariance has a nullspace, preimages are nonunique until a support-orthogonal convention is supplied. If positive eigenvalues approach zero, the inverse square root is generally unbounded and has a proper domain. The total CFC.rpow operation at a negative exponent is therefore not the intended partially defined inverse on all H. Preserve the source unresolved inverse-domain and nullspace convention instead of asserting equivalence of its two displays under every singular interpretation. Do not require beta or theta nonzero merely to define this condition; later ratios dividing by norm(theta)^2 have their own zero-signal issue.

variant_reviews.comparison: For the full training index subset J, average the squared outcome residual times the joint treatment-path indicator, divide by card(J), then add positive lambda_alpha times the l1 norm of every one of the d+1 coefficients. The intercept belongs to that printed penalty; do not silently exempt it. Normalization is by the entire training subset rather than the number following path a; changing the denominator without adjusting lambda changes the objective. Keep the indicator for both treatment times, not propensity weighting or conditional expectation. For nonempty J and finite real data this is a continuous finite-dimensional penalized objective; existence and any selected-estimator measurability are proof obligations rather than consequences of IsMinOn, and uniqueness is not specified. If the path count is zero the printed fully penalized criterion has zero as its minimizer, whereas an empty J raises the distinct source normalization issue. No correctness of the linear working model, random noise law or population minimizer is required just to evaluate this empirical criterion.

variant_reviews.comparison: Start with N=n*K observations in K equal sections of size n. For each i form the empirical probability law of all observations outside section i and evaluate the same functional psi at that law and at the full empirical law, yielding K*psi(P_hat)-(K-1)*psi(P_hat_(i)). This deletes an entire section, not one observation or all but one section. Use indexed multisets to retain repeated values and positive remaining sample size, ordinarily n>0 and K>1; the empirical PMF constructor cannot represent an empty deleted sample. The pseudovalue mean is the arithmetic mean over K. The pseudovalues share most observations and are not independent simply because original sections are independent. No studentization, confidence interval, asymptotic normality or finite-sample unbiasedness is established by this definition.

Then take its real linear span and topological closure in the L2 norm. The tangent set itself need not be a linear subspace or closed, and it is not replaced by all square-integrable functions. Local nonparametricity is the additional equality with L2_0(P) at every model law; it is not assumed for the general theorems. L2 objects are almost-everywhere equivalence classes, so score representatives and the source submodel relation must respect that quotient.

variant_reviews.comparison: Keep the d-dimensional Wiener process and state-independent diffusion matrix distinct from the drift parameter beta. Because Sigma is constant in time and state, the intended integral equation can use x0 plus the ordinary time integral of F(X_s;beta) plus Sigma times W_t-W_0; the Brownian term is not a Lebesgue integral of W. Real Brownian coordinate processes need the appropriate joint independence and compatibility with the supplied complete right-continuous filtration. IsBrownianReal encodes Brownian finite-dimensional laws and a.e. path continuity but has no filtration argument, so adaptation alone cannot be mistaken for independence of future increments from an arbitrary enlarged filtration. The drift time integral needs integrability and a solution path; its totalized definition does not prove existence or uniqueness. Preserve the law's covariance identifiability through Sigma Sigma^T, not uniqueness of Sigma, and keep the stronger Section 2 covariance assumptions separate from this introductory equation. No general stochastic-integral or SDE solution theorem was found in the inspected probability sources.

variant_reviews.comparison: For lambda>0 and candidate lambda_star>0, the positive trace-class covariance gives a bounded scalar spectral function s↦s/(s+lambda_star). Continuous functional calculus can express the corresponding operator after its self-adjointness and spectrum hypotheses are proved; its zero fallback is not a valid substitute. The trace is the sum of sigma_j/(sigma_j+lambda_star), with finiteness controlled by trace(Sigma)/lambda_star. In finite dimensions this is a finite sum, but a matrix trace cannot replace the countable trace-class case. The equation specifies a nonnegative root and asserts uniqueness; generic functional calculus and summability do not prove root existence, uniqueness or selection. At lambda=0 a limit from positive regularization is needed, since lambda/lambda_star can be 0/0 and a covariance with kernel may not have an ordinary inverse. A positive limiting root requires the relevant support-rank regime; ambient dimension exceeding n alone does not establish it. Keep this parameter distinct from later reused kappa and nu conventions.

variant_reviews.comparison: Quantify one probability transition kernel from n observations to n+m observations, allowed to depend on the class and n,m,epsilon but not on the unknown member P. Integrate that same kernel against P^n, take its output marginal and compare its entire joint output law with P^(n+m). The TV convention is half the total variation mass of the difference of probability measures; the unhalved SignedMeasure.totalVariation cannot be substituted directly. The condition requires an attained kernel with uniform error <=epsilon, not merely that an infimum of errors is <=epsilon. Outputs need not retain the original observations, be independent conditionally on the input or be exactly iid; only the unconditional joint law is required to approximate the product law. A deterministic Measure.map alone does not cover randomization. General-space measurability and probability-kernel conditions are required; conditional versions constructed for one particular P cannot be transplanted uniformly without evidence.

variant_reviews.comparison: Retain the finite-population centered zeta products, inverse auxiliary weight X_i^-1, the bar-X/N factor and n*gamma outside expectation. Gamma is the grouping quantity sum N_r(N_r-1)/(N(N-1)), with N>1 and admissible group sizes; c is its n-scaled limit along nu, not a free replacement constant. The second expression centers under the superpopulation law and multiplies a weighted second product moment by c*E_P(X_i). It is not the unweighted covariance or the covariance of a simply centered rescaled variable. Bar-X has no explicit defining main-text equation; its likely finite-population mean interpretation remains a qualification. Positive X_i, integrability of inverse-weighted products and existence of the sequence limits are separate requirements; totalized integration or inversion cannot establish them. The displayed equality of the finite-population limit and superpopulation expression, and strict positive definiteness of the resulting kernel, are not consequences of arithmetic primitives alone. Do not import the high-entropy assumptions of the preceding theorem into this RHC replacement formula.

variant_reviews.comparison: At the specified interior parameter, use densities under the same sigma-finite dominating measure and a measurable vector score. Subtract sqrt(p_theta) and one half of h-transpose times the score times sqrt(p_theta) from sqrt(p_(theta+h)), square and integrate over the sample space. The little-o compares this squared remainder with the squared Euclidean norm of h as h approaches zero within the parameter domain, which is eventually unrestricted locally because theta is interior. Preserve the factor one half, the vector pairing and domination; do not substitute pointwise differentiability of a log density or a scalar derivative. Radon-Nikodym values are extended nonnegative, so real density representatives require the intended a.e. finiteness and nonnegativity, and a nonnegative integral must not use a zero fallback when infinite. This definition at one theta does not assert DQM everywhere, continuous score dependence, nonsingular information or a LAN theorem. Square-integrable score and centered-score consequences need justification rather than replacing the original quotation with stronger conditions.

A positive P mass at a zero R mass gives infinite divergence, not a totalized zero contribution. Require pathwise convergence to zero along nu on a P-superpopulation probability-one event; this differs from convergence in probability or convergence of expected KL. The superpopulation P and sampling-design P(s,omega) are different roles of the notation. The source only names a rejective comparator, without its construction or an explicit matching-inclusion-probability condition; neither is invented. Ordinary Shannon entropy maximization or closeness to a uniform sample law is not a substitute.

variant_reviews.comparison: For a probability measure supported on [0,infinity), the real-measure/complex-argument resolventTransform integrates (t-z)^-1 with the same sign. Nonnegative support belongs to this member, not every grouped empirical law. Negative real z=-lambda with lambda>0 is outside support and gives an integrable resolvent; do not invent an unrestricted complex domain, branch choice or lambda=0 convention from the short definition. A distribution-function notation is interpreted via its measure, not as an ordinary Lebesgue density.

The empirical spectral-law transform on the upper half-plane uses (x-z)^-1 and equals 1/n times the ordinary trace of the matrix inverse A-z I_n. Mathlib resolventTransform supplies the integral with this sign. Matrix.trace and nonsingular inverse provide the matrix ingredients, but the finite spectral trace identity and nonsingularity for the source self-adjoint matrix must be justified; no matching packaged identity was found in the scoped search. The factor 1/n uses the spectral law's matrix dimension, not an arbitrary sample-size divisor from another paper. Preserve the positive imaginary-part convention and include zero eigenvalues with their empirical mass.

G(z)=(H-z I)^-1 and m_N(z)=Tr G(z)/N are defined for the source N by N real-spectrum matrix on the upper half-plane. The source integral has lambda in the integrand but prints mu_N(dz); retain that mismatch rather than rewriting the original formula. The intended measure resolvent has the same (lambda-z)^-1 sign as mathlib. The scalar integral, matrix resolvent and normalized trace are different objects linked by a spectral identity, not interchangeable names. This member's N equals H's size; the separate lower-case trace convention for smaller block matrices does not change this empirical law. General inversion infrastructure does not prove limiting-law assertions.

variant_reviews.comparison: The unprojected leading term is the squared Hilbert-Schmidt discrepancy between T_k(theta) and T_k(theta_star), divided by 2*(k!). Flatten the finite real tensor using the full coordinate-product index type and use the Euclidean sum-of-squares norm; do not use a generic Pi sup norm or restrict the tensor to order two. The discrepancy is between raw moment tensors, not between noisy distributions. This formula is an excerpt defined in a theorem, not an additional assumed theorem conclusion or a complete likelihood expansion. No asymptotic remainder claim follows merely from its scalar expression.

The projected leading term uses tilde-T_k in the projected tensor space, with the same 1/(2*(k!)) scalar. Preserve the projected dependency rather than substitute unprojected T_k or assert the two terms equal. The Hilbert-Schmidt norm is the sum-of-squares norm over all projected coordinates; the general linear Pi is not assumed isometric. Finite tensor coordinates and scalar arithmetic express the formula, but do not prove its leading-order role in the projected likelihood expansion.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use coordinatewise ProbabilityTheory.covariance under F, equivalently the integral of the self outer product of X-E X when the required second moments exist. The application context's two-observation kernel (x1-x2)(x1-x2)^T/2 needs iid copies to have this expectation; it is not an extra input to the covariance definition. The lower-bound theorem separately normalizes diagonal variances to one and selects off-diagonal entries as dependence measures; neither a bootstrap nor jackknife estimator is required to define this population object. Mean subtraction cannot be removed without a zero-mean condition.

The source explicitly assumes E X=0, so the centered coordinatewise covariance reduces to E[XX^T]. The iid sample is used to estimate this population matrix, not to define an empirical matrix or the covariance of contaminated observations. Finite second moments give the intended integrable outer product; a totalized Bochner integral outside integrability would not certify a covariance. Do not add a sample-mean correction to the printed population formula.

Define the mean functional by integrating x and the centered covariance by integrating (x-mu(F))(x-mu(F))^T under F with the required finite moments. F0 and Fn give population and empirical versions of the same functional. For the empirical probability law, the covariance has 1/n normalization, not the unbiased 1/(n-1) correction. Finite covariance alone gives positive semidefiniteness, not positive definiteness or an invertible square root; whitening needs separate nonsingularity. Mathlib's scalar covariance is centered, unlike its separately named uncentered covarianceOperator, so no unnoticed operator-name substitution is made.

variant_reviews.comparison: The estimator divides n^-1 sum_i K_hj(x_j,X_ij)*Y_i by the empirical marginal density n^-1 sum_i K_hj(x_j,X_ij). The boundary normalizer c_h(u) depends on the observation coordinate u=X_ij; it is not a common factor depending only on evaluation x_j and cannot generally be cancelled from all weights. For positive n and nonzero denominator the n^-1 factors cancel, giving the same normalized weighted average. Do not import the conventional translation-invariant kernel in place of the saved boundary-normalized one, or a multivariate product kernel. This estimates E(Y|X_j=x_j), not automatically the centered additive component f_j. Zero-density events have no printed convention here; real-field zero division must not silently define them, even if a later high-probability density bound makes them rare.

variant_reviews.comparison: The time-indexed observation has a constant mean tensor mu, a core tensor F_t transformed by each d_k by r_k loading and an error tensor E_t. PiTensorProduct.map provides the multilinear loading operation after the coordinate tensor identification; retain the mean term rather than absorb it into noise or copy another paper's mean-zero presentation. The displayed model alone does not impose iid or independent cores/errors, orthonormal loadings, or probabilistic identifiability. Main-text tensor descriptions are retained, while appendix-only indexing details are not supplied from another paper.

This member presents X_t=F_t transformed along all modes plus E_t without a separate intercept. Loadings are deterministic d_k by r_k matrices of full column rank r_k, explicitly not required to be orthonormal. Matrix.rank expresses the rank constraint; tensor-product maps give the algebraic transformation. Preserve the source's separately archived core/noise independence and signal context, rather than inferring them from the displayed equality. The lower-bound experiment's orthonormal loadings and scalar lambda are separate restrictions, not attributes of this general model.

For positive k1,k2, ordinary rectangular matrix multiplication gives R F_t C^T+E_t and is the two-mode tensor instance. For k2=0, the source changes the core shape to k1 by p2 and omits C; for k1=0, the core has shape p1 by k2 and omits R; for both zero the signal is absent. These are distinct branches, not products with zero-width core matrices, which would erase the one-way signals. No independent-noise, loading-rank or supplementary B1-B4 condition is invented from this definition; those unresolved external-to-main-text assumptions remain explicit.

The same scalar coefficient sequence a_f,q has sum of squares one and absolute sum bounded by C. Negative innovation times t-q are needed for q>=0; finite observed time range [T] does not truncate the filter. HasSum can state convergence once its topology and summation filter are chosen, for example on an L2 realization; it must not silently impose pointwise convergence at every sample outcome when the source does not specify a version. Absolute summability and finite innovation variance provide ingredients for a convergence proof, not a proof contained in the generic predicate. The iid statement is for each k, not independence across different unfoldings of the same tensor, and not independence of factor and error innovations. variant_reviews.comparison: L1 requires full column rank, r_k=o(T^(1/3)), and a normalized Gram limit as d_k grows. D_k is the diagonal matrix of squared loading-column norms; D_k^-1/2 A_k^T A_k D_k^-1/2 is not whitening by the inverse square root of the full Gram matrix. Full column rank gives positive diagonal entries for the intended nonempty columns. Each diagonal grows comparably to d_k^alpha_k,j, with positive descending exponents at most one; two-sided asymptotic comparability needs both inequalities, not a one-sided IsBigO alone. The limit is positive definite with eigenvalues bounded away from zero and infinity; pointwise PosDef alone does not supply uniform spectral bounds when ranks grow. Since r_k may grow, a single fixed-matrix Tendsto expression needs an explicit common-space or varying-dimension interpretation that the displayed limit does not spell out. Equal strength exponents are allowed, and distinctness is separately imposed in L1-prime. Theorem 2 applies this condition to its selected samples with their local scales, not automatically to the unsampled full-fiber construction.

variant_reviews.comparison: E2 has two separate causal filters a_e and a_epsilon, each square-sum normalized to one and absolutely summable with a common bound C. For each k the two innovation families are independent of each other, and each family has iid centered unit-variance elements over its stated time/fiber/coordinate indices. This is a stronger family-level noise assertion than E1's individual independence clauses, but does not impose independence from factor innovations or between different modes. The resulting processes are weakly stationary, not iid over time; filters with more than one nonzero lag ordinarily create temporal dependence. The infinite past t-q remains part of the construction even when observed t ranges only over [T]. HasSum requires a chosen topology/filter and does not itself prove stationarity, convergence or the variance normalization, or select an everywhere-defined sample-path version. Keep E2 distinct from F1's factor filter and preserve Theorem 2's application to each selected sample.

variant_reviews.comparison: R1 bounds fourth moments uniformly for all factor, shared-noise and idiosyncratic-noise innovations appearing in F1 and E2, including their stated time, coordinate, fiber and mode indices and the relevant asymptotic sequences. For real variables z^4=abs(z)^4. A common finite bound on the fourth-power integral, or equivalently a common finite L4-seminorm bound under the intended laws, expresses this condition. Separate MemLp membership for each variable is insufficient because its finite bound may depend on the index. No Gaussianity, sub-Gaussian tail, bounded support or factor-noise independence is implied. Existing iid assumptions within each family come from the dependencies, not the fourth-moment clause itself. Theorem 2 applies R1 to every chosen sample; do not reduce that to checking only one selected realization.

Do not treat finite covariance alone as positive definiteness or totalized inverse/division conventions as source definitions on singular cases.

The same operations apply after evaluating the mean and centered covariance functionals at the chosen F; keep F dependence explicit and retain the population/empirical specializations. Finite second moments do not make Sigma(F) invertible for every F, especially finite empirical laws, and whitening x at its mean gives zero radius. Additional restrictions or separately declared exceptional-case extensions are needed before a total statistical functional with this polar angle is defined.

variant_reviews.comparison: For finite d, form conditional covariance entries by conditionally integrating products of centered fitted-coordinate errors, multiply by the population covariance and take the unnormalized matrix trace. The outer factor is tau squared/n, and the sample covariance is X-transpose-X/n. The empirical covariance commutes with its own positive-shift resolvent, but not with the population covariance in general; retain the displayed matrix order. The response noise has been averaged out, while this variance remains a function of the design. For the paper's d=infinity branch, Matrix.trace does not supply a trace-class operator trace; the source's trace and finiteness requirements need a corresponding operator construction. Ordinary covariance is unconditional and is only a related centering primitive, not a replacement for the conditional covariance.

variant_reviews.comparison: The two spaces impose both weak periodic divergence zero and zero vector mean; H requires L2 membership, while V additionally requires first weak derivatives in L2. Distributional directional derivatives can represent the componentwise divergence after a periodic function/distribution identification, and the vector integral expresses the mean constraint with integrability. The V inner product is the sum of integrals of derivative products, not the usual inhomogeneous H1 inner product with an added L2 term. Proving it is positive definite and complete uses the zero-mean periodic setting rather than the formula alone. variant_reviews.comparison: Use a Gaussian centered at xi with covariance Omega and weight it by 2*F(alpha_eta(h-xi)); polynomial evaluation and cdf supply constituent functions, and withDensity can weight the Gaussian reference measure. To identify the printed Lebesgue density, require a suitable nondegenerate covariance and the density calculation. Normalization needs the centered Gaussian symmetry, oddness and the stipulated CDF symmetry, not just arbitrary weighting. Preserve the source's open (0,1) wording despite allowed CDF endpoint values, eta=0 issue, and covariance validity only on its specified high-probability event; a non-PSD input to multivariateGaussian collapses to a Dirac measure and is not a paper-approved fallback.

This member centers the rescaled coordinates at the MAP and uses the inverse of the negative likelihood Hessian divided by n, not the full posterior Hessian. Its skew polynomial is homogeneous cubic with the original third likelihood derivative and 1/(12*eta*n*sqrt(n)) factor. Generic Gaussian/CDF/weighting APIs leave the random curvature event, positive-definite density domain and coefficient identities to prove; they do not convert an arbitrary constrained MAP into an interior stationary point or identify this density with the projection-centered approximation.

The Gaussian covariance is the CC block and the skew function uses the separately derived marginal polynomial with both linear and cubic terms. The formula is F of the conditional mean polynomial, whereas integrating the joint density produces the conditional mean of F of that polynomial; these generally differ. Preserve this as a separate approximation, including arbitrary C with its unstated empty/full-block conventions. Gaussian pushforward or total-variation contraction alone cannot establish equality of these densities or the marginal approximation rate.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use the Bernoulli law with first atom 1 of mass 1-pi0 and second atom 0 of mass pi0. A binary probability kernel assigns to each indicator its unit-interval density law; composing the indicator measure with that kernel gives a joint indicator/p-value law, and iid copies express the model across hypotheses. The alternative density integrates to one on [0,1] and is common across indices; the null is the uniform density on that interval. The marginal density pi0+(1-pi0)*f1 is interpreted on the unit interval, with zero density outside its support, not a positive constant on the entire real line. Keep pi0 endpoints: a zero-probability indicator branch has an irrelevant conditional version, rather than requiring both branches to have positive mass. The real CDF agrees with the displayed integral for thresholds in [0,1] and saturates outside; expectations average both indicators and p-values. Do not import the separate alternative-shape condition.

variant_reviews.comparison: B1 needs both unconditional process weak convergence and conditional bootstrap weak convergence in probability to a centered Gaussian process with C*min(abs(s),abs(t)) times the same-sign indicator; IsGaussianProcess alone gives neither covariance nor path regularity. B2 uses one beta<q+1, one high-probability event A_n shared by two unconditional expectation bounds, and a supremum over V in [1,a_n*delta]; it does not impose beta>0 or substitute conditional expectations. B3 and B4 distinguish original-versus-population and bootstrap-versus-original global consistency, with additional a_n-scaled local Phi bounds on the closed neighborhood. B5 gives lower endpoint inequalities with o_P errors, not equalities. B6 separately requires nonnegativity, monotonicity, right continuity, both range endpoints and closed truncated ranges. B7 controls left jumps at sqrt(n*a_n) scale; Function.leftLim has a point-value fallback when no limit exists, which cannot be used to conceal absent source-domain/left-limit conventions. Convergence-in-measure and deterministic Big-O APIs do not supply the missing process-space construction, nor justify adding iid sampling or a particular resampling scheme.

variant_reviews.comparison: Sum Var(V_i,j) over all p coordinates at a fixed time. Under the zero-mean null this is the expectation of the squared Euclidean norm even with cross-coordinate dependence, not the variance of a coordinate sum. The real variance API maps infinite extended variance to zero, so finite second moments must be established. Keep the exact center separate from the approximation 2p/(bn) and from an expectation evaluated at a selected random time.

Restrict the same c_j by the indicator j in L_s and sum over j=1,...,p. Set.indicator and finite sums preserve this coordinate-set restriction without introducing a square-root-cardinality divisor; that divisor belongs to the later statistic. Do not replace an arbitrary source neighborhood subset by a contiguous interval unless separately assumed.

Sum Var(V_i(ell)) over B_s intersect L0 for the general spatial contrast under its zero-mean null. Cross-location correlations do not add cross terms to the expectation of a sum of coordinate squares. Retain the general model's sigma convention and observed-site index set, rather than replacing this by the linear-model approximation or treating it as variance of an aggregated scalar contrast.

variant_reviews.comparison: IsCaglad on the interval subtype [alpha,beta] expresses exactly left continuity and right-hand limits, with one-sided endpoint conditions relative to the interval. This is not IsCadlag, whose side conventions are reversed. Build the path subtype and supremum metric using boundedness of these real paths on the compact interval, then generate the sigma-algebra specifically from metric balls. Do not assume this ball sigma-algebra is the entire Borel sigma-algebra for the supremum topology: the path space is not generally separable in that metric, and arbitrary open unions need not be countable ball unions. The source instead asserts equality with the Borel sigma-algebra for a Skorohod metric. No Skorohod construction or that measurable-space identification was found in the pinned tree. Ordinary bounded continuous-function spaces exclude jump paths and therefore cannot replace this space.

variant_reviews.comparison: For the stated measurable nonnegative density h, the requirement is integrability of x -> |x|^q*h(x) under Lebesgue measure, or equivalently finite q-th absolute moment of the identity under the probability law with density h. MemLp at ENNReal.ofReal q encodes the latter with its measurability requirement, and q>=1 ensures a positive finite real exponent. Merely comparing a real-valued totalized Bochner integral to infinity does not express finiteness, because nonintegrable inputs have integral zero in Lean. Preserve q=2 where Theorems 1,2,4 require it and general q>=1 in Theorem 3; Theorem 5 does not inherit this assumption. Heavy tails do not mean that all moments, or even the second moment under the general q premise, exist.

Keep the separate first-stage weighted ell^1 term and terminal ell^K=ell. variant_reviews.comparison: Represent approximately equal random folds I_v and population subsets J_k explicitly, with fixed V. Fit conditional odds out of fold on ([n] minus I_v) intersect J_{k+1}, classifying target against relevant sources using the history. In contrast, the displayed algorithm fits pi^a from observations inside I_v; retain this despite the preceding blanket out-of-fold prose and the optional alternative in Remark 2. Set terminal ell^K to the fixed loss and regress backward from K-1 to 1 using the already fitted next-stage response on the same specified out-of-fold populations. Compute each in-fold pseudo-loss mean, then weight fold estimates by |I_v|/n; an unweighted average is not exact when sizes differ. Empty folds, absent training classes and estimated zero denominators need the recorded source qualifications. This main-text Algorithm 1-dagger is distinct from the supplement's general Algorithm 1 and the later feature-shift Algorithm 1; its motivating DS.0-dagger label does not erase the theorem's drift analysis under model failure.

The map is identified as an efficient influence function only at true nuisances and r_*, under DS.0 and the paragraph's density ratios uniformly bounded away from zero and infinity. Generic nuisance choices do not imply zero mean or efficiency. Integration supplies an expectation operation, not regular asymptotic linearity or tangent-space optimality; the excluded supplementary regularity definitions remain excluded.

Use the odds pseudo-loss and the centering denominator pi^0(1+theta^0), with theta^0 defined from the source-population marginal odds. Equivalence with D13 requires the exact nuisance transformation and first-population identity on their proper domains. The efficient interpretation additionally uses true nuisances, target inclusion under DS.0-dagger and bounded odds from the identifying paragraph. Do not propagate those qualifications into every theorem branch or infer a unique regression version under model failure; arbitrary supplied nuisances still define the displayed algebraic map.

variant_reviews.comparison: Take m=n delta_n as a positive integer, with n=2^N in the surrounding setup. Build the noise as the log of the average of m squared jointly independent standard Gaussian variables; gaussianReal 0 1 gives each marginal and iIndepFun is joint independence rather than pairwise independence or identical distribution. Positivity of the sum of squares holds almost surely for m>=1 and justifies the ordinary log and exp inversion; mathlib's log on nonpositive inputs does not supply the source's statistical conventions. To identify the observation, use the blockwise constant volatility identity for the Brownian increments and the source-normalized sigma_0^2=1, together with independence of the price Brownian driver and fractional-Brownian driver. Preserve the block index i<delta_n^-1 and integer degrees of freedom n delta_n. No appendix trigamma formula or replacement observation grid is introduced.

variant_reviews.comparison: The threshold families depend on both gamma and delta. Under the premise that the empty set is not in Psi, require admissibility of the resulting chi-star procedure for every pair in (0,1)^2, and separately require log A_e equivalent to |log delta| and log B_e equivalent to |log gamma| for every e along their joint approach to zero from above. Admissibility is a global finite-error requirement, not a consequence of asymptotic calibration. Keep the source procedure's admissible positive threshold domain so real logarithms represent the intended quantities. The statement allows any threshold family satisfying both properties and does not prescribe one specific sufficient bound from Theorem 3.1.

Divide by sigma_0 to obtain the population autocorrelation. The autocorrelation inference branch has the lower bound sigma_0>c. This is weak stationarity, potentially for a triangular array changing with T, and does not require a linear AR data-generating model or strict stationarity.

Use sigmahat_j=T^-1 sum_{i=j+1}^T X_i X_(i-j) and sigmahat_0=T^-1 sum_{i=1}^T X_i^2 in the ratio. Do not replace it by a sample-mean-centered Pearson correlation or use the lag-dependent T-j denominator. Population nondegeneracy does not define every sample when all observations vanish. The source does not specify the resulting zero-denominator value; totalized field division must not be presented as a supplied statistical convention.

Use both bootstrap autocovariances from the same joint multiplier vector, including the random perturbed lag-zero denominator, and restrict the requested lags to I. Do not leave the denominator at the unbootstrapped sigmahat_0 or reuse the population lower bound to claim bootstrap positivity. The Gaussian perturbation may give a zero or negative lag-zero estimate and need not generate a PSD covariance sequence, so the ratio need not automatically lie in [-1,1]. The original source leaves its zero-denominator case unspecified; conditional-law inference and outer probability rates are not part of the bare ratio equality.

The statistic here is the uncentered maximum from (2.2), not the later centered estimation-error statistic.

Condition on X and the row response Y^(j), keeping the estimated scale, M and empirical Gram covariance fixed, then use the centered Gaussian law with covariance sigmahat_j^2 M Sigmahat M^T. For n>0 the empirical Gram is PSD and congruence plus the squared scale preserve PSD, permitting a singular Gaussian measure as well. multivariateGaussian otherwise has an irrelevant Dirac fallback; it is not a proof of this covariance condition. Take the maximum of |Z_jk| over E contained in a single row {j} times V2, then the conditional P_Z quantile at 1-alpha. Do not multiply that Gaussian maximum by another sqrt(n), pool rows into an unspecified joint law, or replace the data-dependent conditional law by an unconditional Gaussian. variant_reviews.comparison: Order all d-1 off-diagonal magnitudes within each row in descending order with multiplicities preserved, and at each s<=k_tau define E_j^(s) by the non-strict <= comparison with the s-th largest magnitude. Finset.sort on distinct values would lose multiplicities; one can sort indexed entries using a deterministic index tie refinement without changing these magnitude thresholds or their inclusive tie sets. Take the maximum of the inverse-quantile scores over s; the source leaves what c-hat inverse means, including discontinuity/tie behavior, unspecified, so it cannot be silently replaced by a survival probability. Then sort alpha_j ascending, include alpha_(0)=0, choose the largest j satisfying alpha_(j)<=qj/d and select every alpha_j at or below alpha_(jmax), returning empty when jmax=0. Require valid d and k_tau ranges for these order statistics. The printed square graph excludes diagonal entries; its rectangular response-by-predictor use in Section 4 is a retained missing adaptation, not an invitation to invent one. These algebraic operations alone do not establish FDR control.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each integer k from zero through m, count p-values satisfying the non-strict comparison p_i<=alpha*k/m, retain candidates whose count is at least k, and choose the largest candidate. This is a step-up rule, not the first passing threshold or a step-down procedure. The construction itself needs neither independent nor valid null p-values, whereas an FDR guarantee requires its own statistical hypotheses. variant_reviews.comparison: Use the conditional law of H_i given the observed p-value and evaluate it on the null event H_i=0. In the supplied two-groups model, uniform null density on [0,1] makes the Bayes numerator pi0, so the ratio is pi0/f(t) where the mixture density is positive and its version is fixed. This is the posterior probability that the null is true, not the reversed description recorded from the abstract and not the global FDR of a rejection procedure. Conditioning on a continuous observation is represented by a regular conditional kernel, not division by the probability of the singleton event p_i=t. The kernel's characterization is almost everywhere under the observation law. At mixture-density-zero points, particularly possible when pi0=0, the displayed ratio has no uniquely determined statistical value; Lean's total division or a chosen kernel version does not resolve that source convention. The identity requires the Bayes/density calculation under the given model rather than following from condDistrib's existence alone.

variant_reviews.comparison: Keep four Boolean predicates on DMAGs, interpreted as truth conditions and then reflected into Bool if desired. A_D(M) asserts existence of a ts-DAG with M equal to its observed finite-window latent projection, equivalently membership in the projection map's image once that map exists. A_D^stat instead uses the stationarified projection; the source explicitly warns that this resulting class need not be the class of ts-DMAGs, so the first two cases are not equated. A_ta combines time order with repeating ancestral reachability; A_to combines time order with repeating marked orientations, not repetition of all adjacencies. Directed time order permits same-time arrows since the inequality is <=. The needed latent projection preserves ancestral and separation information, which Set.image alone does not construct or prove. Do not add stochastic stationarity, causal Markov/faithfulness or finite maximum edge-lag premises to these graph predicates.

variant_reviews.comparison: Form sum_{j=1}^d Pi_j composed with F as an ambient-space operator; starProjection has the correct codomain, unlike a projection whose output is only the subspace subtype. Under the eigenspace properties this equals the sum of lambda_j Pi_j over the retained distinct eigenvalues. The archived Pi_j projects onto the whole eigenspace for the j-th distinct eigenvalue, whereas the dotted sequence counts eigenvectors with multiplicity. Thus the formula can retain more than d individual components unless the appropriate simple-spectrum conditions apply; do not replace it with an arbitrary basis-vector cutoff. Finite nonzero eigenspaces of the compact self-adjoint operator admit the needed projections. The empirical version uses the sequential estimator's own corresponding eigenspaces, not fixed population projections, and retains its eta/index/denominator issues. Spectral completeness alone does not provide ordered eigenvalue selection, uniform eigengaps or the trace-class process limit and differentiability arguments used downstream.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use AntitoneOn for f1 on the unit interval, allowing flat portions. In the nondegenerate mixture 0<pi0<1 with the positive mixture-density version, pi0/(pi0+(1-pi0)*f1) is nondecreasing exactly when f1 is nonincreasing. variant_reviews.comparison: The candidate density averages a Gaussian of mean Pi*g*theta and covariance sigma^2 times the identity over the supplied rotation law Lambda. Preserve the projected output dimension in the normalization and exponent denominator, and take the unprojected case by Pi=identity with dimension d. The group-averaged density is a Gaussian mixture, not generally a single Gaussian whose mean is the group-averaged mean. R_n is the negative mean sample log-density, whereas R is its expectation under the fixed true law p_(theta-star), not the candidate law p_theta. Equality E[R_n]= -E[log p_theta(Y)] requires the common marginal law and integrability; it is not a definition of expectation under the empirical law. The intended Gaussian density requires sigma>0 and a Euclidean norm, and logarithmic positivity/integrability must be justified rather than using Real.log(0)=0 or the Bochner integral's zero fallback. The generic Gaussian law declaration does not itself provide this exact Haar-mixture density formula or its differentiability.

variant_reviews.comparison: Index the product law by triples (t,i,j) with t in [T] and 1<=i<j<=n, and assign each coordinate Bernoulli-rho with inclusion atom first. The product construction uses probability measures and yields joint independence across all observed edges and layers. It is not a law on two independently sampled symmetric entries or on self-loops; reverse entries of a displayed adjacency matrix are the same observation and the diagonal is not modeled here. There are no community or layer labels under this null. Both testing hypotheses are compared on the observed graph tensor, not on an enlarged sample containing latent labels. Endpoint rho values can define degenerate Bernoulli laws even if later likelihood-ratio results need interior parameters.

variant_reviews.comparison: Quantify over a sequence of measurable binary tests on the observed graph tensor and require the sum P1(test=0)+P0(test=1) to tend to zero along the given model sequence. The tests may vary with n; a fixed test for all dimensions is not required. The two errors use their respective laws on the same observation space, with latent assignments marginalized rather than supplied to the test. On probability measures both terms are finite and nonnegative, so their real-valued sum is legitimate and vanishing forces each error to vanish. This defines strong detection, not exact community recovery. Its negation says no such vanishing-error sequence exists and does not by itself imply total variation tends to zero or that every nontrivial weak test fails; the paper's separate chi-square theorem supplies stronger evidence in its own regime.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use Set.pi over the full coordinate index set to select an arbitrary tuple of coordinate laws from their respective families, then map that tuple to the product probability measure. The model class is the image of these law tuples, not merely a Cartesian product whose elements are tuples rather than joint distributions. Similarly theta ranges over the unrestricted Cartesian product of the Theta_j and its law is the product of p_(theta_j). Coordinates may have different spaces and families; no common scalar parameter, identical distribution, exponential-family form or continuity is built into this definition. Every selected law must be a probability measure, since infinitePi returns zero otherwise. Independence concerns coordinates of one observation; an i.i.d. sample of n observations requires a separate product construction. Later existence of two parameter points at a given Hellinger scale does not establish continuity of the entire parameter map.

variant_reviews.comparison: Reset the Xi_1 or Xi_2 block index to t minus the preceding stage endpoint on each left-open/right-closed stage interval. Sigma searches additional times s>=0 with Gamma>=b, whereas tau searches s>=1 with the stage-restarted product of likelihood ratios <=1/d; retain these non-strict tests despite the prose saying exceeds. An acceleration stage ends after sigma(b1); a detection stage ends after min(sigma(b2),tau), and a tie counts as successful detection. The final N is the first successful cycle, and T-tilde=S_(2N), not the first arbitrary stage endpoint. hittingAfter can express each relative-time crossing after constructing its process at the random stage start, but proving stopping/predictability requires the observed filtration and appropriate adaptedness, not access to the latent state. Nat.find can select N only after existence of a finite successful cycle is proved. The source does not fully define infinite stage endpoints or all zero-duration recursion cases; no arbitrary zero/default treatment or infinite-time arithmetic is inserted.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use square-integrable real functions under the stated measure on the bounded domain, then quotient by almost-everywhere equality to obtain the definite L2 norm and Hilbert-space interpretation. MemLp.toLp explicitly constructs that equivalence class; the literal set of measurable functions has only a seminorm because distinct representatives may differ on null sets. The source does not state the quotient or all underlying measure-space conventions, so record this as a required interpretation rather than silently rewriting its definition. eLpNorm represents the higher-p expression in extended nonnegative reals and retains possible infinity. Membership in L2 on a bounded domain does not imply finite Lp norm for p>2; even finite-measure embeddings apply in the opposite direction. Do not use conversion of infinity to real zero to claim a finite norm, and pointwise evaluation of later random functions requires representative conventions separately.

variant_reviews.comparison: For the loading matrix, the source G_k stores descending eigenvalues of A_k^T*A_k, hence squared singular values of A_k; its square root is the diagonal singular-value factor. A right Gram eigenbasis and square roots provide the components, and for positive singular values the paired left vectors are A*v/sigma. Rank-deficient cases need orthonormal completion instead of dividing by zero, while this loading context supplies its own full-column-rank conditions. Keep Q_k=A_k*D_k^(-1/2) separate: equality of its column span with A_k requires invertibility of the diagonal normalization, and its normalized-Gram limit is a model assumption, not an SVD consequence. Eigenvectors are only specified up to signs and rotations under repeated eigenvalues.

Preserve the two rectangular decompositions as sums of singular-value-weighted outer products, with lengths min(p,n-1) and min(p,n), and the corresponding leading-r left frames. The spectral primitives supply ordered values and Gram eigenbases, but the paired left/right vectors and exact reconstruction must be assembled, including zero-singular-value completions when needed. The library values are zero-indexed and padded by zeros; the source's finite sequence does not automatically adopt that extension for sigma_(r+1) at its last allowed r. Keep that endpoint issue and unspecified measurable/tie selection. The two matrices differ by a column, but their chosen bases need not be aligned or have matching signs.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each of the full and leave-one-column-out observed matrices, use an eigenbasis of its left Gram operator and select the requested leading directions in descending singular-value order. These are empirical data subspaces, not singular vectors of the rank-at-most-k signal matrix P. The permission r in [k] does not alone prove r is within both finite SVD lengths; preserve the saved dimension/endpoint limitation rather than silently padding the frame with extra vectors. Zero-padding scalar singular values does not supply such vectors. Signs, repeated-eigenvalue rotations and measurable selection remain unspecified, and a truncation through a tied singular value need not define a unique subspace.

The LSVD_m output can be built from the first m columns of a descending left-Gram eigenbasis for its supplied input matrix. It requires an admissible truncation dimension and an orthonormal output frame; it is not the list of scalar singular values. A chosen eigenbasis is not unique under ties, and a spectral tie at the cutoff can change the selected subspace. The noncomputable existence of an eigenbasis does not establish a measurable algorithmic selection for the paper's random matrix input. Keep the original operator and its input choices, without adding signal-rank or eigengap conditions from later sufficient assumptions.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each subject use the function-valued model mu_i plus delta_i times the strict event t>tau_i plus the error. The change therefore starts after tau_i, not at it; subjects may have different mean functions, jumps and break locations, and a zero jump represents no effective break. Temporal stationarity is a separate property of each error process, not independence across time or subjects. Under distributional stationarity it can be expressed by IdentDistrib of every finite time block and its admissible shift, not merely equality of one-time marginals; do not replace it by i.i.d. errors. If only a weaker moment-stationarity convention is intended, that must remain a separate interpretation rather than silently strengthening the source. The standing function-space quotient and moment qualifications remain applicable, and no common break or cross-subject independence is introduced.

variant_reviews.comparison: Compute sign(sign(x) times max(|x|-lambda,0)), or equivalently return sign(x) when |x|>lambda and zero otherwise. Equality at the threshold is zero, and a zero input stays zero; retaining only sign(x) or using >= would change boundary behavior. The output is ternary {-1,0,1}, not the soft-thresholded real magnitude that appears inside the outer sign. Real.sign has sign(0)=0 and the positive-part identity supplies the scalar maximum, so their elementary case analysis gives the stated form, including Q_0=sign. Apply the same operation independently to each coordinate; this is not vector-norm thresholding, stochastic rounding or a privacy mechanism by itself.

variant_reviews.comparison: Each machine j computes its own mean with denominator n_j over H_j, applies the coordinatewise Q_lambdaN threshold and sends one ternary vector to the trusted server. Unequal machine sizes of comparable order are allowed; replacing n_j with a common N/m changes this recipe. Call the archived DPVote on the m vectors with the given selection count and privacy parameters. Its dependency first peels noisy stability maxima without replacement using epsilon/2 and delta/2, then samples selected signs with probabilities proportional to exp(epsilon-prime times the corresponding utility/4), where epsilon-prime has its separately specified factor 4 sqrt(2 s-tilde log(2/delta)). PMF.ofFintype can encode the three positive normalized sign masses but supplies neither the peeling noise nor privacy composition. Preserve the score/utility distinction, unresolved noise-independence/tie conventions, and coordinate association/zero extension needed to turn the returned support and sign set into a vector. Privacy is for replacing one entire machine dataset in the trusted-curator setting, not record-level protection or hiding the messages from that server. variant_reviews.comparison: Color each of the n vertices independently and uniformly from K+1 colors, or use the uniform law on all functions Fin n→Fin(K+1) and prove its independent coordinate law. Colorfulness on V is InjOn mu V, requiring distinct colors for every pair of distinct vertices, including nonadjacent pairs. A graph's ordinary proper coloring only separates adjacent vertices and would be insufficient. For |V|=K+1, the favorable restricted assignments are bijections to the color set, counted by (K+1)! after identifying the two finite types; the total number is (K+1)^(K+1). This yields the displayed r, with K a nonnegative integer and a nonempty color set. The stated r is not the probability for arbitrary subset cardinalities. The coloring law is auxiliary algorithmic randomness independent of the graph data, not a coloring selected adaptively after observing edge weights.

variant_reviews.comparison: Set t=ceil(1/r) and generate 2t independent colorings, with one array for A and a separate array for B, independent of the observed graphs. variant_reviews.comparison: Under P_i absolutely continuous with respect to Q for each i, form the vector of RN derivatives P_i.rnDeriv Q and push the resulting measurable vector map forward under Q. The object gamma is this joint law, not the vector-valued function, a product of its marginal laws, or its law under one of the null P_i. Mathlib derivatives take extended nonnegative values; because each P_i is a probability measure and P_i<<Q, the derivative has Q-integral one and is finite Q-almost everywhere. Passing to a real nonnegative vector therefore needs an almost-everywhere finite version, with arbitrary changes only on a Q-null set. This yields coordinate means one, not independence or square integrability of the coordinates. Without AC, rnDeriv would describe only the absolutely continuous component and the mean-one conclusion could fail. variant_reviews.comparison: For a function whose domain is the subtype O, HasCompactSupport means its nonzero support has compact closure in O, preserving compact support within the open domain rather than merely compact ambient closure touching its boundary. Combine this with the appropriate smoothness or source function-space membership. The source's C(overline O) explicitly means uniformly continuous functions on O; replacing it by arbitrary ContinuousOn O would weaken that convention. H_c^k consists of compactly supported members, whereas H_0^k is the completion of smooth compactly supported functions in the H^k norm. They are not interchangeable, and the continuous dual used in Theorem 11 retains the inherited H1 norm on H_c^1. The inspected whole-space Fourier/Bessel-potential Sobolev predicate does not directly establish these domain spaces or identify their closures.

variant_reviews.comparison: Represent a nontrivial closed half-space by a weak affine linear inequality and its closed complement by the opposite weak inequality, so their intersection is the boundary through x times the all-one vector. This is not set-theoretic complementation, whose intersection would be empty. Preserve exclusion of the whole positive diagonal, inclusion of minus-one, and both normalized barycenter constraints. For a genuine split require mu_x to be a submeasure of gamma so the positive remainder gamma-mu_x recombines with it; library measure subtraction by itself is truncated and does not certify domination. Without N, boundary mass may need allocation and restricting gamma to both closed sides can double-count it. Under the hyperplane-null condition N, boundary mass vanishes and the source asserts unique split measures and the restriction formulas; it does not assert a unique half-space. Existence is stated without N. No generic hyperplane-separation result identified here proves the two barycenter conditions, and the source's zero-mass barycenter case stays unresolved.

The source's interpretation as the difference of the two population expectations uses integrability of the individual outcomes; integral_sub provides that algebraic identity under its hypotheses. variant_reviews.comparison: Represent p_i as an [0,1]-valued adapted variable and, for each law in its individual null H_i, bound the CDF of its pushforward law by x for every x in [0,1]. This includes the endpoints as printed. Adapted requires measurability at the current information field, and marginal null validity does not imply conditional superuniformity given the past, mutual independence of p-values, or validity of every intersection-test construction without its separate assumption. Pushforward measurability must be established rather than using its total fallback.

For the nonnegative variable X, impose the null CDF bound at every alpha in (0,1), and equality at all those thresholds under every null for exactness. For each alternative Q require the reversed weak inequality at all thresholds and a strict inequality at some threshold which may depend on Q. Do not exchange the for-each-Q and exists-alpha quantifiers or reduce power to improvement at a single common threshold. Truncation at one leaves events {X<=alpha} unchanged for the stated open threshold range. This member carries no filtration-adaptation condition from the online-paper variant.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use the finite real expansion with frequencies one through K, one cosine and one sine coefficient per frequency, each basis function divided by sqrt(pi). This gives exactly 2K real coefficients and no constant mode, with mean zero and the standing K>=2 restriction retained. The inspected Fourier basis is complex exponential and orthonormal under normalized Haar measure, whereas the source real trigonometric basis is orthonormal for ordinary Lebesgue integration on [-pi,pi). Finite sums and real trigonometric functions construct the source expansion directly, with no infinite-series convergence issue.

variant_reviews.comparison: Construct independent latent angles with normalized Lebesgue law on [-pi,pi) and independent standard Gaussian noise vectors in Euclidean 2K-space, independent also across samples, then push forward by rotated signal plus the fixed known positive sigma times noise. Normalized restriction via cond expresses the angle law because the interval has finite positive Lebesgue mass. Conditional on each angle the observation is Gaussian with mean g(alpha) theta and covariance sigma squared times identity; after integrating out the angle it is generally a Gaussian mixture, not one Gaussian vector. Preserve N independent observations, the full 2K coordinates and one shared angle per observation, rather than assigning independent angles to frequencies or estimating sigma by default.

variant_reviews.comparison: Retain an independent pair consisting of a random probability mixing measure with Dirichlet-process law based on a finite positive H0 and a positive scale with law Pi_sigma. Integrating the centered Gaussian kernel against the random mixing measure yields the signal density, and convolution with the fixed error density yields the observation density. The base measure H0 need not have total mass one: its total mass is the Dirichlet concentration and cannot be discarded by normalization. The random mixing measure need not itself possess a density. Gaussian kernels and convolution are available, but a prior law on probability measures with the Dirichlet finite-partition distributions was not located in the searched probability modules. Base-density and scale-tail restrictions remain separate assumptions, and no posterior contraction claim follows from the mixture constructor.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use the positive-definite H to define the weighted vector length sqrt(x-transpose H x), and contract the real symmetric tensor with k copies of a weighted-unit vector. The source takes the supremum of the signed contraction with no absolute value. This cannot generally be identified with the standard multilinear operator norm for even k: for k=2, H=I and T=-I, the repeated-vector supremum is -1, whereas allowing two independent unit vectors gives supremum 1. Therefore preserve both printed formulas and the source's claimed equality as an unresolved assertion, without inserting absolute values or certifying a norm. Matrix positivity, finite contractions and conditional suprema can express the printed quantities; they do not prove that equality. Also keep arbitrary nonsymmetric matrix products used elsewhere outside this symmetric-tensor definition.

variant_reviews.comparison: Define s1 as the maximum row sum of pointwise absolute kernel suprema over both coordinates, then define the discrepancy with the composition order (I+Theta)(I+Pi-hat). The alternative expression (I+Theta)(Pi-Pi-hat) uses the inverse identity (I+Theta)(I+Pi)=I and is not automatic for a formal total inverse. Mathlib's inverse returns zero outside continuous-linear equivalences, so actual invertibility must be supplied. The magnitude delta-tilde_jk at u_j is the L2 norm of that kernel section in x_k alone, not an induced operator norm or a supremum over u_j. Ordinary inverse kernels with finite row suprema are not furnished by abstract operator invertibility, and identity Dirac kernels cannot be treated as ordinary bounded functions. Keep pointwise rather than essential suprema and finite-section conditions; A7's extra derivative bounds are not required just to name these quantities.

variant_reviews.comparison: Define p^h at each point as the expectation over the sample randomness of the empirical smoothed density, then marginalize in all coordinates except j over the unit cube. This is a deterministic expected smoothed density, distinct from the true density p and the random density p-hat, with its own h dependence. The marginalization identity follows from the empirical identity after a justified expectation/integration interchange: nonnegative Tonelli or integrable Fubini with the required joint measurability. The inspected Fubini theorem supplies the latter interchange but does not prove the empirical density's normalization or measurability hypotheses. Use withDensity only with the correctly interpreted nonnegative density, and preserve the separately recorded p_j^h defining equation rather than replacing it by p_j or p-hat_j.

variant_reviews.comparison: For p0335 (2.5), retain the hierarchical prior, disjoint model tags, parameter map T and likelihood p_n(T(theta),Y). Build the normalized withDensity measure on positive finite evidence. posterior supplies a conditional-law kernel after proving standard Borel/nonempty parameter space and finite measurable sampling kernel; its almost-everywhere density theorem is not an unconditional samplewise identity or a convention at zero/infinite evidence. It does not select a variational minimizer.

For p0519 (16), form the dependent Markov-path likelihood product p_D,f(X_(i-1)D,X_iD), retaining the explicit joint Borel measurability and B in S. The initial law is common to all parameters; its cancellation does not make path observations iid. Identify the sampling kernel’s predictive-relative density with this likelihood divided by its prior integral before applying posterior_eq_withDensity. Keep f coordinates distinct from theta coordinates used for other posterior expectations, and justify the version when evaluating under a fixed true diffusivity law.

For p1433 D11, posterior directly provides the structural conditional law of f given X once the function parameter space is nonempty standard Borel and the model is a measurable finite kernel. Dominated Bayes formula requires the corresponding measurable density representation and normalizer identification. The paper analyzes the result under fixed P_f0^(n), not the prior predictive law; an almost-everywhere posterior identity under the latter does not alone justify every true-law statement or supply function-space posterior contraction.

For p1691 D12, the prior is on probability measures on R^d and may depend on n. Use the n-fold product convolution-density likelihood f_Y(Y_i), not a likelihood for directly observed signals, and prove measurability of the law-valued parameterization and positive finite evidence. The regular-kernel construction needs the corresponding standard Borel realization; posterior_eq_withDensity gives a predictive-almost-everywhere identity after density identification. Later posteriors of observation laws require a measurable convolution pushforward rather than a new prior or silently identifying signal and observation laws.

For p1825 (21), weight the Gaussian prior on initial states V by exp(-one-half the sum of squared Euclidean R^2 residuals) and supply its marginal normalizer. Keep the source u_theta(X_i,t_i) argument ordering as printed, including the recorded discrepancy with model (19). The resulting kernel is a posterior for the nonlinear PDE observation experiment after measurability/space proofs; the generic constructor does not assert it is Gaussian or prove MCMC behavior. Its defining conditional-law equivalence is almost everywhere under the model marginal and needs the appropriate version for fixed P_theta0^N analysis.

variant_reviews.comparison: For p1178 use the unconditional complete test-pair law P_Q for (X,Y), set mu=Measure.map X P_Q and eta(x) to the conditional-label kernel mass at {1}. The feature domain is R^d and the label space is binary; do not condition eta on the missingness pattern or replace X by its zero-filled observed projection. The kernel is a probability distribution and yields the correct regression identity almost everywhere. Later missingness and smoothness conditions are imposed at all support points, so the library’s arbitrary values on null fibers do not by themselves satisfy those pointwise conditions or resolve the source version convention.

For p1433 retain X in [0,1]^d, d≥1, and independent observations from the common pair law. h0(x) is the success mass of condDistrib Y X under that law; the ordinary definition does not require a logistic prior, though a later map constructs one. Use the appropriate cube subtype and measurable coordinates. The binary conditional law can be represented as bernoulliMeasure 1 0 h0(x) after bounding the kernel mass, but independence of sampled pairs remains separate from the one-pair conditional law. No multivariate wavelet basis or dimension-dependent contraction rate is supplied by these APIs.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each fixed alternative g, the inner infimum/max is an absolute-error decision problem for the location Z(h), h in {f,g}, under the white-noise laws with noise epsilon; only afterwards take the supremum over g. minimaxRisk uses extended nonnegative risk and the correct inf-estimator/sup-parameter order for that inner problem, but its estimators are all Markov kernels. Establish equivalence with the paper's admissible estimator convention or restrict explicitly to deterministic measurable functions; do not assume randomized and deterministic optimization coincide. One estimator is shared by the two laws, but may depend on the fixed pair because its infimum is inside the outer supremum. Preserve infinite risks using lintegral; no attainment or global inf-estimator/sup-all-functions equality follows.

Instantiate the two-point absolute minimizer-location loss with the fixed-design Gaussian regression sampling law on n+1 observations and noise sigma. Its outer supremum over g remains outside the pair-specific estimator infimum. The generic minimaxRisk quantifies Markov-kernel estimators; identification with the printed infimum needs the estimator-class bridge, and an extended integral avoids giving nonintegrable losses the Bochner fallback value zero. Do not substitute the white-noise experiment, squared loss or one estimator optimized uniformly over the entire convex class.
