variant_reviews.comparison: Construct the empirical probability measure for positive sample size as n^{-1} times the sum of Dirac measures at the observed full triples, and use its integral for the empirical functional. Point evaluations give the finite average; n=0 does not produce a probability law by this formula. The population expectation needs a function on the actual joint sample support even though the prose says a function on R. Keep that recorded domain issue. The printed Lp formula uses f(z)^p without absolute values, whereas eLpNorm uses the norm of f; these are not generally equal for signed f or arbitrary real p. Agreement requires a justified domain such as nonnegative f (or appropriate even integer p), not a silent insertion of absolute values. The uniform norm is an ordinary supremum of absolute values over X, not an essential supremum; real supremum lemmas need nonempty bounded value sets. Bochner expectation likewise needs integrability to avoid its fallback zero. The source formula remains preserved with these qualifications.

Integrate exp(A*(h-u))*Sigma*Sigma^T*exp(A^T*(h-u)) over [0,h] to form Omega_h; for nonnegative h the integrand gives a positive-semidefinite covariance after proving the relevant matrix identities and integrability. multivariateGaussian provides the centered innovation law with this covariance, but positivity must be proved rather than relying on its fallback Dirac law for non-PSD inputs. Keep the printed remainder R(h,x_0) after the h and h^2 terms in (6), not a substituted cubic remainder.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each diagonal Bernoulli coordinate, compute E(d-p)^k with d=1 of probability p and d=0 of probability 1-p. This gives p-p^2, p-3p^2+2p^3, and p-4p^2+6p^3-3p^4 for orders 2,3,4, respectively. Assemble these bounded finite moments as diagonal matrices; ordinary powers of diagonal matrices act coordinatewise. The superscript (5) denotes P^(4)-3(P^(2))^2, a fourth-cumulant expression, not a fifth raw or centered moment and not necessarily nonnegative. Keep p_j as observation probabilities and retain their dimension dependence in the later P_n notation. These expectation identities only require the coordinate Bernoulli laws, while independence is additional model information; no division by p_j or uniform positive lower bound is part of this entry.

variant_reviews.comparison: Extract the diagonal of the projected sample covariance at the specified iteration m+1 and mode k, take reciprocal positive square roots coordinatewise, place them on a diagonal matrix and multiply on both sides. Matrix.diag EXTRACTS a vector while diagonal BUILDS a diagonal matrix; these two operations must not be confused. Positive sample diagonal entries are needed for the intended unit-diagonal correlation matrix; Real.sqrt at a negative number and field division at zero are totalized, not source-approved fallbacks. Preserve the source sample covariance and iteration index, rather than substituting the population-style fixed-direction formula inside Theorem 8. The saved zero-variance and direction-selection qualifications are not resolved by algebraic normalization.

Use the diagonal population variances to form D, and define correlation by inverse-square-root diagonal congruence under their positivity. Then recover Sigma=D^(1/2)*R*D^(1/2) by cancellation. The earlier positive-definite population covariance supplies the appropriate population domain, whereas diag(S) is only a proposed estimator of D and can still have zero entries. Modeling R^{-1} concerns the precision of the correlation, not the correlation itself; its inverse relation to Sigma^{-1} needs invertibility. Keep D unrelated to the theorem-specific D0/D1 matrices and do not carry population nondegeneracy over to arbitrary sample estimates.

Normalize the pooled sample covariance S on both sides by the reciprocal square roots of its OWN diagonal, retaining the sample definition and its groupwise centering. On strictly positive sample variances the coordinate formula is S_ij/sqrt(S_ii*S_jj), with unit diagonal; zero sample variances can occur under permitted discrete observations despite a positive population covariance. Do not use totalized inverse/sqrt values to claim a valid correlation matrix at those samples, and do not silently add a ridge or replace sample variances by population variances. Even with positive diagonal entries the sample correlation can be singular, so downstream inverse modeling requires further conditions.

variant_reviews.comparison: Take the real infimum of K times the singleton arm probability over every arm and EVERY covariate in the target support, not the source support or only observed covariates. With K>0, nonempty target support and a normalized finite-arm kernel, the value set is nonempty and bounded below by zero; at any supported x, at least one arm has probability at most 1/K, giving the upper bound one. The conditional infimum lemmas then apply with these premises. No strictly positive exploration or attained minimizer over x is asserted, and the infimum is not an essential infimum. Values of a behavior kernel outside its source-almost-everywhere determination matter here; preserve a specified version on the full target support rather than treating arbitrary disintegration extensions as equivalent.

variant_reviews.comparison: At candidate beta, sum only over j with beta_j nonzero by using the indicator of Function.support beta. Keep omega^e/4 times the square of coordinate j of the population risk gradient, summed across environments. This enforces selected linear moments, which are weaker than full conditional-expectation invariance; the nonzero-coordinate gate is exact and generally discontinuous at zero.

For each nonzero candidate coordinate, form the empirical mean of x_j^e times the candidate residual separately in each environment, square that mean, then sum with omega^e. This is not a mean of squared per-observation products, nor the square of an environment-pooled mean; opposite environment moments should not cancel the penalty. The source permits positive normalized weights and different n^e in this method definition. Use explicit empirical finite sums; no population derivative or expectation can replace them. Preserve the same exact support gate and do not substitute the smooth Gumbel approximation mentioned for numerical practice.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use the underlying Brownian noise of the white-noise experiment together with the two independent auxiliary Brownian motions, retaining the displayed affine coefficients and the common deterministic integral drift. The three coefficient rows have squared norm three and are mutually orthogonal, so their normalized linear combinations have covariance min(s,t), continuous paths and joint Gaussian finite-dimensional laws. The inspected process-level theorem proves mutual independence once cross-covariances vanish for ALL s,t across distinct output processes; independence only at each common time would be insufficient. IsBrownianReal additionally requires almost-sure continuous paths and is indexed by nonnegative times, so restrict to the source interval [0,1] rather than assert an unprovided extension of interval-only processes. The resulting observation noise scale is sqrt(3)*epsilon. This is randomized orthogonal splitting of one observed process, not partitioning design points or asserting the three generated observations are independent of the original Y.

variant_reviews.comparison: For a fixed f in F integrate z -> ell(f,z) against P, not the empirical distribution of the observed data and not a posterior over hypotheses. The later bounded-loss condition is |ell(f,z)|<=1, allowing signed losses; with measurability this ensures integrability under a probability law and the ordinary real integral is appropriate. Do not use ENNReal.ofReal without nonnegativity, because it would discard negative values. Evaluating this deterministic risk function at the random empirical minimizer is a later operation, not a change of its definition.

Integrate the specific nonnegative Huber loss ell_tau(Y-f(X)) under the joint law of X,Y, retaining tau in (0,infinity]. The source loss (2.7) uses one-half times the squared residual in the central region, so the tau=infinity case is one-half squared loss even though the prose calls it squared loss. Use the finite-tau Huber definition or an explicit infinite-tau branch, not arithmetic involving an infinite real cutoff. Bochner integral matches a finite population risk under the relevant moment and function-class conditions; the nonnegative lintegral preserves infinite risk outside those conditions. This risk is neither its empirical average nor excess risk relative to f0.

For the joint observed law P_star of (Z,A), take the measurable event s={A=0}, require positive event probability, and integrate ell(Z) against ProbabilityTheory.cond P_star s. This produces a scalar target risk, not the random-variable conditional expectation on the entire sigma-algebra of A. The conditioned measure is a probability law only with positive finite event mass; its zero fallback at P_star(s)=0 must not invent a target risk. General ell is real-valued, so signed integration requires integrability under the target conditional law; nonnegative risk can instead retain infinity through lintegral. The predictor or prediction set used to construct ell is given, not optimized in this definition.

Use the separate target probability law Q and integrate ell directly under Q, even when no observed datum has target label zero and the observed label set omits zero. Conditioning P_star on an absent event would give a null measure and is not this estimand. Identification from source distributions via the later sequential-conditional assumptions is separate from defining expectation under Q. Keep Z general and multiple source populations permitted, with signed integrability or the applicable nonnegative extended-risk treatment.

For each environment law mu^e integrate the squared REAL residual |y-beta dot x|^2, retaining candidate beta and the population law. The finite moment assumptions support integrability for the intended real-valued risk; otherwise use the nonnegative extended integral rather than Bochner zero fallback. This environment risk has no one-half factor, differs from the empirical average, and is not pooled over environments. The statement here consistently uses beta; do not import the printed x-for-beta ambiguity from the later population EILLS formula (3.8).

For each client k and fixed common parameter theta, integrate xi -> f_k(theta;xi) under that client’s own P_k. Neither the losses nor their laws are assumed identical across clients. Keep each F_k separate from the weighted federated risk F, its empirical version, and its optimizer; expectation under a mixture or an unweighted pooled law would change this definition. General real-valued client losses require integrability for finite risks; lintegral applies only when a nonnegative loss is actually given, not by silently truncating signed loss values.

variant_reviews.comparison: Build a three-point noise law with probabilities beta at -1, 1-alpha-beta at 0 and alpha at +1, using alpha,beta in [0,0.5] to ensure nonnegative total-one weights. The indicator formula replaces the edge by zero, preserves it, or replaces it by one respectively; it is not a Bernoulli XOR with one common flip probability. Under a fresh-noise release-kernel interpretation the conditional flip probabilities are alpha for input zero and beta for input one. Independence among the noise coordinates alone does not prove independence from X, and the source leaves that latter point implicit; keep the displayed conditional identities and the saved qualification. Sample one noise per permitted edge and mirror it for undirected graphs, never draw the two orientations independently. Neither a privacy guarantee nor recovery of X follows just from this construction.

Use the same three-point channel on the ALREADY released Z with weights delta,1-2*delta,delta, retaining strict 0<delta<0.5 and theorem-specific sequences delta when applicable. Independent noise over unordered edges is mirrored symmetrically. Conditional on a fixed first-stage graph, a fresh-noise interpretation defines the bootstrap channel and sequential PMF composition, but independence from the first-stage data is an implicit source convention rather than an explicitly quoted hypothesis. The second graph is neither an independent original beta-model draw nor generally independent of Z. Do not promote this sampling construction to a conditional bootstrap limit theorem or replace the population centering/scaling in the paper's later results.

variant_reviews.comparison: For a measurable statistic T, the deterministic kernel from X to T supplies the theta-X-T direction. The theta-T-X direction requires one conditional reconstruction kernel for X given T that is independent of theta and gives the correct JOINT disintegration under every P_theta; matching a single marginal law is insufficient. When theta is a fixed model index, replacing it by a constant random variable makes conditional independence vacuous, so do not use that as a sufficiency proof. A randomized parameter formulation can use CondIndepFun under a specified joint prior/model law, but one prior's almost-everywhere identity alone does not certify the required parameter-uniform family. condDistrib needs its regular conditional existence hypotheses and only selects versions under a given law; the saved arbitrary-space and cross-parameter version issues remain. No dedicated matching sufficient-statistic declaration was found in the searched Decision/Kernel modules.

variant_reviews.comparison: Represent the gradient expectation as zero and the Hessian expectation as S^{-1}, both evaluated at m+S^(1/2)Z with the SAME standard Gaussian Z and V=n*v. The gradient and derivative-of-gradient give the Euclidean Hessian after a fixed basis identification; differentiability and Gaussian integrability of the derivative fields must be established before using the totalized derivative/integral objects. S is symmetric positive definite and its square root is the positive symmetric root, not an arbitrary factor such as a Cholesky matrix; use CFC on that domain and a genuine matrix inverse. These two equations define stationarity, not an attained global KL minimizer, uniqueness or selection of the canonical solution. The later restriction to R_V and its existence/uniqueness result are separate, and the cited external calculation is not imported as a proved local theorem.

This defines a solution-selection region and does not assert every pair in it solves the first-order equations.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use a deterministic kernel for T_n, a Markov kernel for the source’s possibly randomized f, and a kernel from the target statistic space to the full (n+m)-sample space. Composition integrates over the intermediate randomness; a deterministic pushforward alone would omit it. The reconstruction kernel must be independent of the unknown parameter and have a compatible conditional version on statistic values that f(T_n) can attain. A condDistrib selected under one P0 is only specified almost everywhere under that P0 statistic law, so the source’s suggestion to use any P0 requires justification. Neither existence of individual conditionals nor their composition proves the stated TV equality or an executable sampling algorithm.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use EuclideanSpace R (Fin d) modulo its integer-coordinate additive subgroup. The quotient norm is an infimum over coset representatives, and the distance of classes is the norm of their difference; this gives inf_k ||x-y+k|| with the source Euclidean norm. The integer lattice is closed and discrete, so prove metric nondegeneracy and that the infimum is attained to recover the printed minimum; the generic quotient norm theorem does not assert attainment for arbitrary subgroups. Use [0,1)^d only as a representative convention, not the ordinary distance between those fixed representatives. A plain product of circle metric spaces generally has the product supremum metric, so it is not automatically the paper's Euclidean quotient metric without an L2 metric construction.

variant_reviews.comparison: Represent the quotient probability by a Borel measure on R^d that is invariant under every integer translation and has mass one on the half-open fundamental cell [0,1)^d. Such a periodic measure generally has infinite total mass for d>0; do not identify it with a probability measure on the whole Euclidean space or push the entire lift forward as though it had mass one. Restrict to one fundamental cell before mapping to the quotient; conversely use a measurable representative and periodic extension, checking boundary ownership so integer translates neither omit nor duplicate mass. The absolutely-continuous subclass means the periodic lift is absolutely continuous with respect to Euclidean Lebesgue measure. Equality with a formulation using quotient Haar measure requires the appropriate correspondence and normalization, not a silent replacement of reference measure.

variant_reviews.comparison: Let rho=P+Q, p=dP/drho and q=dQ/drho. Both probability measures are absolutely continuous with respect to rho, so no singular mass is lost; their RN derivatives are finite rho-almost everywhere and can be converted to real values for the square roots. Set H=sqrt((1/2)*integral (sqrt(p)-sqrt(q))^2 drho), justifying integrability, which holds for probability measures via the bound by a constant times p+q. This includes mutually singular distributions and yields H=1 in that case, unlike normalization without one-half. Do not use P.rnDeriv Q alone to discard the singular part or conflate H with H squared.

variant_reviews.comparison: For every coordinate j, require two parameters in its own Theta_j whose SQUARED normalized Hellinger distance lies in [1/(10*n),1/(5*n)]. Choose the pair separately for each j and allow dependence on the given n. Keep the product structure from Theorem 6.4 without importing that theorem’s additional TV premises. variant_reviews.comparison: Restrict the objective to measurable maps of the TORUS pushing P forward to Q, and integrate the squared quotient Euclidean distance from x to T(x). Using periodic Euclidean representatives requires integration over a single half-open fundamental cell, not over the infinite periodic lift. The compact torus bounds the cost for measurable maps, but feasibility and existence of an optimal map do not follow just from that bound. IsMinOn expresses the objective inequality and must be combined with membership in the admissible transport-map class; it does not itself assert pushforward equality, attainment or uniqueness. Preserve the source absolute-continuity restrictions on both measures and do not substitute Euclidean displacement of arbitrary lifted representatives for the torus cost.

variant_reviews.comparison: Represent phi_0 as a finite-valued convex potential on R^d whose gradient induces the optimal map on the quotient, retaining uniqueness only P-almost everywhere. The convex lift is not a periodic scalar function: its quadratic correction has the source periodicity, and the gradient has the corresponding integer-translation equivariance where defined. ConvexOn and gradient express these objects, but a gradient outside differentiability uses a library fallback and must not become an asserted everywhere transport map; measurable representatives and almost-everywhere differentiability need justification. No inspected declaration supplies the torus Brenier theorem, pushforward optimality or almost-everywhere uniqueness. Keep the source conjugate-domain and additive-constant conventions separate, rather than imposing an unprinted normalization or Euclidean-cost theorem with different hypotheses.

variant_reviews.comparison: Right-multiply each standardized innovation design by the same deterministic covariance square root, keeping n,n_z,n_w row sizes and a shared p-column covariance. Preserve iid real innovation entries with zero mean, unit variance and finite fourth moment; no Gaussian law or rotation invariance is implied. The common constants 0<c<=C bound the FULL covariance spectrum uniformly over p, equivalently positive-semidefinite differences from c*I and C*I. CFC.rpow can choose the positive symmetric square root on the positive-definite domain; do not interpret nonnegative square root as merely entrywise nonnegative entries or silently choose a nonsymmetric factor. Sigma_ii=1 fixes population variances, whereas finite-sample column standardization is a data-dependent operation and need not preserve the exact iid-innovation representation. Preserve the source equivalence claim as a flagged qualification, not a proved identity.

variant_reviews.comparison: Form the probability measure assigning mass 1/p_l to each eigenvalue of the real symmetric population block, indexed with multiplicity, and evaluate its closed lower half-lines to obtain the printed ESD. The positive dimension is needed for total mass one. The library eigenvalue enumeration is sufficient after identifying the matrix with its self-adjoint Euclidean operator; ordering does not affect the ESD. ProbabilityMeasure weak convergence expresses the assumption on each growing block and on the whole population covariance. Weak convergence does not assert CDF convergence at every discontinuity of H_l or H; preserve the source wording without strengthening it to pointwise convergence at all x. These are population spectral laws, not the separate sample spectral distributions. A mixture expression for the whole limit requires the block-weight limits and their appropriate finite-block regime; it is not supplied by the weak-convergence primitive.

The formula inserts no sample-mean correction, and the sample matrices can be singular. The word approximated alone is not a norm-consistency theorem in this high-dimensional regime.

Use the external reference columns W_l and denominator n_w in the same uncentered Gram and block-diagonal construction, retaining the reference panel as a separate data object with aligned variant columns. Reindex the dependent block sum to the source column order. Neither replacing n_w with n nor assuming that a finite reference Gram matrix is positive definite is justified. Independence and approximation guarantees are separate model/theorem statements, not consequences of the blockDiagonal' operation.

Use the testing columns Z_l and denominator n_z in the uncentered Gram construction before block assembly and column reindexing. The testing data are reused for this estimate; this is not an independent external reference matrix merely because it shares the same algebraic formula. Preserve the distinct data role, possible singularity and absence of an empirical centering correction. No consistency assertion follows from matrix multiplication or block assembly alone.

variant_reviews.comparison: In the Euclidean one-sample setting, define phi0(x)=norm(x)^2-2*varphi0(x) and psi0(y)=norm(y)^2-2*varphi0_star(y), with conjugation as the preceding source supremum over Omega. The factor two and source/target order are essential. The map is gradient varphi0 where differentiable; generic gradient/ConvexOn does not produce a Brenier optimizer. These corrections must be shown integrable and dual-optimal. Additive constants in the Brenier potential change the two corrections oppositely; the source supplies bounded representatives in this section, not a universally mean-zero convention.

The same algebraic formulas are applied to the convex lifted potential on R^d in the torus two-sample setting. The lift varphi0 itself is not periodic; norm(x)^2/2-varphi0(x) is periodic, and this is what lets the corrected potential descend to the torus. The transported map is interpreted modulo Z^d, with the equivariant lift supplied by the transport result. The main text does not separately specify the conjugation domain for this lifted torus use after the earlier Omega-restricted definition; retain that source issue rather than silently choosing a global or unit-cell conjugate. Dual optimality and appropriate periodicity of both corrections require the torus transport theorem.

variant_reviews.comparison: An infinite orthonormal complete wavelet family belongs in a HilbertBasis of the appropriate real L2 space, rather than a finite-dimensional OrthonormalBasis. The registered HilbertBasis identity applies only after such a basis is constructed and completeness and orthogonality are proved; MemLp.toLp embeds measurable square-integrable representatives into the almost-everywhere quotient. No Daubechies or wavelet construction was located in the inspected Analysis/Probability search. Retain the Euclidean scaling functions, dyadic normalization, translations and detail indices 1 through 2^p-1 separately from the periodized family and its explicit constant mode. variant_reviews.comparison: Work on the nonnegative half-line with a smooth real tau, AntitoneOn tau there, tau(x)=1 for x<1/2 in its domain, and tau(x)=0 for x>=1. Do not replace smoothness by the discontinuous indicator I(x<1); the surrounding text explicitly says the analysis needs a smooth cutoff. Nonincreasing behavior and the plateaus ensure values between zero and one. This definition specifies an admissible function and does not require a particular bump-function formula or the later spectral eigenvalue weights.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each sample size T retain an integer-indexed mean-zero weakly stationary process with finite second moments. The centered library covariance then equals the printed product expectation, and lag invariance gives E[X_i X_(i-j)]=E[X_0 X_(-j)]. Without the zero-mean assumption, this uncentered expectation would not be covariance. The allowed dependence of the underlying process on T must be represented explicitly rather than forcing one fixed infinite process for all sample sizes. No strict stationarity or independent increments follows. This source passage belongs to the Section 3 autocovariance setting and must not be imported into Theorem 1's more general nonstationary products.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use the joint symmetric experiment (Lambda,Y) and squared Frobenius loss for the Gram matrix Lambda Lambda^T, normalized by positive n squared. The Frobenius matrix norm must be selected explicitly; the default matrix norm need not be Frobenius. The source writes a minimum and separately asserts posterior-expectation attainment. condExpL2 is an orthogonal projection and supports the least-squares argument when the Gram target is square integrable; transferring it to a measurable function of Y requires the observation-sigma-algebra factorization. Fourth-order control of Lambda entries is a sufficient finite-dimensional target-L2 condition and must be checked in the admitted prior hypotheses rather than supplied by a totalized condExp. Use nonnegative extended expectation for risks outside a justified finite domain. The primitive does not prove attainment or the experiment-specific MMSE value by itself.

Use the asymmetric experiment (Lambda,Theta,A) and infimize normalized expected squared Frobenius error over measurable matrix estimators of A. This is the same Gram loss as the symmetric member but a different observation experiment and prior dependence, so equal loss definitions do not imply equal risks. Preserve an infimum rather than silently asserting an attained minimum. Nonnegative extended integration avoids interpreting nonintegrable real losses as zero; finite-risk or posterior optimality arguments require their own target moment conditions. The later sub-Gaussian/third-moment comparison assumptions are not inserted into this definition. Neither condExp nor generic conditional L2 projection alone proves the asymmetric-to-symmetric comparison.

variant_reviews.comparison: Condition on the entire observed vector (X1,...,XT), using its generated sub-sigma-algebra. E-star of an integrable bootstrap quantity is condExp with respect to that sigma-algebra; Prob-star of an event is the conditional expectation of its indicator, or the event mass under a regular conditional bootstrap kernel. It is not conditioning on an equality event with positive probability assumed, and not merely conditioning on a fitted statistic. The conditional value is a random function of the observed data; the bootstrap randomness is integrated out. On the finite probability space setting the trimmed measure is finite, but measurability and integrability still need to be satisfied rather than using condExp’s zero fallback. Conditional kernels identify versions only almost everywhere under the data law, not at every imaginable sample vector.

variant_reviews.comparison: For the given positive bandwidth k_T form C[j1,j2]=K((j1-j2)/k_T) on indices 1,...,T and use the centered Gaussian law with covariance C. K(0)=1 makes each marginal variance one; the vector is generally correlated, not T independent standard Gaussians. Nonnegative entries and symmetry alone do not imply PSD: the source’s nonnegative integrable Fourier transform provides the missing quadratic-form argument. Singular PSD covariance is allowed; positive definiteness is not required. multivariateGaussian maps a non-PSD input to a degenerate fallback, so checking PSD is essential to assert the prescribed covariance. variant_reviews.comparison: Use the time-dependent measurable causal functions g_t and iid driving zeta_t from (10), on a product space carrying an independent copied driving sequence. Replace only innovation t-s, retaining every other past input; the earlier block-replacement recipe also explicitly leaves the history unchanged when the replacement time is in the future, so negative lag gives zero. At each positive real q use eLpNorm of Z_t minus its coupled version and take the supremum over ALL integer t. q may be below one: this is a moment quasi-seminorm, and no norm triangle inequality with unit constant may be assumed. The source uniform q-moment bound ensures coefficient finiteness, but cumulative Delta_(m,q) additionally sums lags s>=m for integer m and need not be finite without a tail assumption. Use an extended nonnegative sum or prove summability before a real tsum, rather than turning a divergent tail into a default zero. Do not import the stationary covariate model, its supremum over unit vectors, or a fixed-time stationary simplification into this scalar nonstationary variant.

For p>=1 and lag k>=0, replace epsilon_(i-k) by its independent identically distributed copy in the SAME function g_i, leaving the rest of the entire causal history unchanged. Product coordinates give an explicit coupling and IdentDistrib specifies equality with the original innovation law; an independent copy of the output X_i would instead replace too much randomness. Take the Lp effect and supremum over i, since g_i can vary with time and stationarity cannot reduce this to time zero. The coefficient itself does not include the cumulative Theta tail or an additional polynomial weight, both defined separately later. Positive finite moments or extended-valued suprema must be handled explicitly. Keep this innovation replacement distinct from mixing coefficients and from a block replacement of the entire past.

Index product innovations by time and a copy flag, assigning both flags at time i the law of e_i; this allows independent but NONIDENTICALLY distributed original innovations. The copied sequence is jointly independent and independent of the original sequence, with each e_i^dagger having its own corresponding law. For k>=0 replace exactly input e_(i-k) in g_(i,j), while k<0 is explicitly defined to leave X_(i,j) unchanged. Define the individual Lm difference for m>=1 and then take a supremum over both time i in Z AND coordinate j=1,...,d. The vector coordinate supremum is not the supremum over all unit-direction projections used by a different source definition. Copy identity and the zero-negative-lag convention hold row by row when the process depends on sample size T; no common time-invariant g or innovation law is imposed. Retain extended values until the relevant uniform moment bound establishes finiteness.

variant_reviews.comparison: Construct the class of real functions on R whose supremum absolute value plus Lipschitz seminorm is at most one, and take the supremum of the signed integral difference. The class is closed under negation, so this signed supremum agrees with the absolute-difference version after proving that symmetry; the displayed source need not be rewritten. Preserve the SUM norm convention, not separate bounds of one or a max norm, which yield a different numerical metric. Boundedness ensures integrability under probability measures and a bounded objective; zero is an admissible test. LipschitzWith and the bounded-continuous supremum-norm identity express the pieces. The Portmanteau theorem tests convergence separately against all bounded Lipschitz functions; it does not directly assert that the supremum over this normalized class metrizes weak convergence, nor uniformity for two varying laws. In particular the normal approximation may depend on n and must not be recast as convergence to a fixed normal law.

variant_reviews.comparison: Choose c>0 and an integer l0 uniformly, then for each admissible sample size n and l with l>=l0 and 1<=l<=n require every j=1,...,n-l+1 to satisfy norm_L2(sum_(r=j)^(j+l-1) X_r)^2/l>=c. The source leaves n implicit in the displayed condition; preserve the nonempty-block domain rather than assigning a minimum to an empty range or a reciprocal at l=0. On mean-zero square-integrable processes this norm squared is the block variance, but finite second moments must be checked before converting extended L2 values to reals. Form S_i_plus by summing X_j_plus minus ITS OWN expectation from j=1 through i. This is winsorization/clipping, not deletion of observations exceeding b, and E[X_j]=0 does not imply the clipped mean is zero. The threshold uses total sample size n rather than the running index i. Bounded clipping gives integrability on a probability space, so the center is well-defined. Preserve the distinction between covariance of uncentered clipped variables and second moments of their centered partial sums, as used in the separate approximation statements.

variant_reviews.comparison: Retain the causal process (1.2), p>2, Theta_(0,p)<infinity, some A>1 and a finite positive C such that every i>=0 satisfies (i+1)^A*Theta_(i,p)<=C. Because the weighted values form a nonempty bounded-above real set after finiteness is established, csSup_le_iff identifies this all-lag bound with the printed supremum mu_(p,A)<=C. The weight is (i+1)^A and applies to the TAIL sum, not merely delta_p(i). Do not replace the uniform bound by a limit at infinity, an eventual bound without handling initial lags, or a time-averaged condition. No covariance nonsingularity assumption is included in this dependence condition, and the term norm does not by itself supply a library normed-space instance.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use Q_n=sum over 1<=s<=t<=n of a_(s,t)*X_s*X_t with |a_(s,t)|<=1 and a_(s,t)=0 for |s-t|>D_n. The sums and ceiling require a positive INTEGER D_n<=n, although the display only explicitly states D_n<=n. For k=1,...,ceil(n/D_n), group terms by t from (k-1)*D_n+1 to min(k*D_n,n), and for each such t sum all s=1,...,t; the band constraint automatically removes distant terms. R_k is the sum of V_j-E[V_j] for j<=k, not the leftover linear block variable R_j defined earlier in (3.1). Dependence across blocks is allowed; finite second moments ensure each product expectation exists.

For each delta>=0 and u, define Psi_K(u;delta) as the supremum of |K(y)-K(u)| for |y-u|<=delta, including both endpoints. variant_reviews.comparison: For a C2 function on the stated smooth manifold, require every constrained critical point to be either a global minimizer on the manifold or to have a tangent direction with strictly negative Hessian quadratic form. In a local chart, vanishing first derivative and the second iterated derivative provide a coordinate formulation; at a critical point the sign property is invariant under valid smooth chart changes, but proving that identification remains necessary. Restrict derivatives to tangent/chart coordinates rather than taking the ambient Hessian on normal directions. IsMinOn expresses the global value inequality and must be combined with membership in the manifold; it does not supply existence of a minimizer. Strict negativity must not become nonpositive curvature, and global benignity does not assert unique minima, nondegenerate minima or convergence of an arbitrary optimization algorithm. The source least-eigenvalue notation can be related to a negative direction in the finite-dimensional self-adjoint Hessian setting.

The reported theta_hat is the intercept because g_(h,0)(0)=(1,0), not evaluation of the fitted slope at treatment zero relative to the current a. IsMinOn over all R2 expresses the optimizer predicate, while a weighted Gram inverse expression needs its nonsingularity and the kernel hypotheses giving the intended least-squares problem. Use deterministic weighted sums S_j(t)=sum_(i=1)^n (t-t_i)^j*K((t-t_i)/h_n) and response X_i. The explicit weights are K((t-t_i)/h_n)*(S2-(t-t_i)*S1)/(S2*S0-S1^2); no 1/h_n normalization appears in these sums. variant_reviews.comparison: After equipping the admitted probability-measure space with the correctly defined convex-order relation and proving its partial-order properties, Maximal (membership in N) mu says mu belongs to N and no strictly larger distinct feasible measure dominates it. IsGreatest N mu instead requires membership and domination of every member of N. Their generated dual definitions use only an LE relation; antisymmetry is the extra property that turns mutual comparability in Maximal into equality, so it must not be skipped for an inadequately defined convex order. The generic greatest-element predicate includes feasibility even where the source prose abbreviates it. A maximal measure can be incomparable with another maximal measure, and neither constructor proves existence. Preserve the SHINE theorem's maximality guarantee unless a maximum is independently established.

variant_reviews.comparison: Fix null i, put alternative p-values at zero and p_i_prime=1/(ell+1), and draw the OTHER null coordinates iid CONDITIONAL on the common U. U has ell+1 iid Uniform(0,1) coordinates with descending order statistics, so the other p-values are generally dependent after U is integrated out. On 1/(ell+1)<=x<1 the displayed CDF uses 1-U_(floor(x*(ell+1))+1); below that interval it is zero and at x>=1 it is one in the intended indicator-restricted reading. For L=ell+1>=2 this gives mass 1-U_(2) at 1/L, masses U_(j)-U_(j+1) at j/L for 2<=j<L, and mass U_(L) at1, which telescope to one. For L=1 the intended law is concentrated at1. Preserve the original indicator expression and its out-of-range subscript issue: multiplication by zero is not a formal definition of an invalid indexed term. A justified piecewise construction is a comparison interpretation, not a replacement source transcription. The resulting law depends only on i,m,ell,H0, not the unknown observation densities.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each graph node j in[d], let psi_j be its binary rejection decision and count false rejections only where the TRUE node degree is strictly less than k_tau. Divide that count by max(1,sum_j psi_j), then integrate under the graphical-model data law. Degree equal to k_tau belongs to the alternative, and the hypothesis family is nodes, not individual edges; retain the graph’s node-set convention in the bipartite and undirected settings. If no node is rejected the numerator is zero and denominator one, so FDP=0 without any undefined division. The displayed numerator’s upper d and H0 notation mean summing over null nodes within[d]. No library ingredient proves StarTrek’s control at level q merely from this definition.

Use the joint law P of all training and test observations and the measurable test-index rejection set R(Z) subset{1,...,m}. The true-null set consists of TEST indices whose marginal P_i equals P0, not the calibration index set or a set determined by estimated density equality. FDP is card(R intersection H0)/max(1,card R), and FDR is its expectation over the full data law, including any dependence and the score-fitting data. Empty R gives exactly zero. Because the random ratio is bounded in[0,1], it is integrable once measurable; do not replace E of this ratio by a ratio of expected counts or a conditional-bootstrap expectation.

At each fixed theta in R^n, let phi_i(X) in{0,1} be the measurable rejection decision, count the decisions at coordinates satisfying theta_i=0, and divide by max(1,sum_i phi_i(X)). Integrate with respect to the data law at that fixed theta; this is a frequentist expectation, not an average over a prior on theta. The null set is parameter-dependent and differs from a graph-degree or distribution-equality null. Empty rejection gives zero and the ratio is bounded, so ordinary probability integration applies. A sequence of procedures may depend on n, but that convention does not change the finite-n definition or imply asymptotic control.

Distinct polynomials are Gaussian-orthogonal, but repeated equal entries are not distinct orthogonal elements. variant_reviews.comparison: Generate iid feature vectors from N(0,I_d), with conditional logistic labels, and use a proper centered Gaussian prior with covariance Sigma where its inverse-density expression is valid. The posterior precision contribution is theta^T*Sigma_inverse*theta/2 in n*v; equivalently it is divided by2*n in v, while ell is the negative likelihood average over n. Features are observed/conditioned on for posterior inference; their theta-independent density cancels from posterior normalization but still determines frequentist random-design probability statements. A singular covariance needs a different support/reference interpretation and cannot be inserted into the ordinary full-dimensional inverse-density formula by a singular matrix default. The source’s formal Sigma_inverse=0 flat prior is not an actual Gaussian law with finite covariance; use a flat Lebesgue-reference likelihood and prove a finite positive normalizer when applicable. Do not confuse this prior Sigma with the later posterior covariance denoted by the same letter.

variant_reviews.comparison: Under the canonical hatpi=N(mhat,Shat), let A=E_hatpi[third derivative V(X)] and contract it entrywise with (1/2)*(x-mhat) tensor Shat-(1/6)*(x-mhat)_tensor3. The positive one-half covariance term and negative one-sixth cubic term are essential. This is a scalar signed correction to expectations, not automatically a nonnegative density factor1+Q or a normalized probability distribution. The expected third derivative is taken at Gaussian-distributed X, not at mhat, and V=n*v supplies the n scaling. Tensor-integrability and the finite coordinate contraction must be justified; generic iteratedFDeriv does not provide the approximation remainder theorem.

In the logistic model V=n*ell plus a quadratic prior term, so its third derivative is the SUM of psi_triple_prime(theta^T X_i)*X_i_tensor3 with no residual1/n, and the Gaussian prior contributes zero to this third derivative. The coefficient b_i(theta)=E_(theta~hatpi)[psi_triple_prime(theta^T X_i)] uses theta both as an apparent free argument and as the integration variable: for fixed data and hatpi the resulting coefficient is constant in the theta where Q is evaluated. Preserve the printed notation collision instead of giving it a new data-dependent/free-variable interpretation. The contraction yields sum_i b_i times [(1/2)*X_i^T(theta-mhat)*X_i^T Shat X_i-(1/6)*(X_i^T(theta-mhat))^3]. The Xi are observed design vectors held fixed in these Gaussian expectations; averaging over their design law would change the correction.

variant_reviews.comparison: Starting at the four-regime fit, retain the printed initial SSR's free K as a source issue. At K=4,3,2 compute the minimum merged two-region SSR minus the existing two-region SSR for each adjacent pair, choose an argmin, merge and relabel, and set S_T(K-1)=S_T(K)+D_T^(K). This reaches K=1 even though the later prose lists only 2,3,4. The final choice minimizes log(S_T(K)/T)+(lambda_T/T)*K over all 1<=K<=4; log at zero SSR requires a convention not supplied by totalized Real.log. IsMinOn needs membership and attainment separately, and says nothing about efficient fitting, tie-breaking or matching relabeled estimated regions to true labels. Do not replace the greedy candidate sequence by optimization over all possible partitions or extend the inherited K0<4 theorem scope.

variant_reviews.comparison: For T>0 compute ehat_t=epsilonhat_t/sigmatilde(X_t,Z_t), subtract the sample mean of ehat, and map the uniform probability law on Fin T to the resulting centered residuals. This Ghat is a residual distribution, distinct from the calligraphic boundary-minimizer set.

variant_reviews.comparison: Preserve independent covariate and residual resampling as stated, followed by the four-regime fitted response with beta-hat_k and gamma-hat^c, LSE refitting, averaging N boundary minimizers, and B repetitions. A product probability law can encode the chosen independence once genuine component laws are defined, but Step 1's Ftilde versus earlier F0tilde naming and the printed CDF orientation need resolution. The source supplies neither a law for the N minimizers nor an N asymptotic guaranteeing their average is a Lebesgue centroid; an arbitrary solver selection is not sufficient. The final empirical pairs are centered at the original estimates and scaled by T for gamma and sqrt(T) for beta. This model-based independent resampling is not a block bootstrap, and the generic constructors do not prove its consistency.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use the law of (Lambda,Y) against law(Lambda) times law(Y), with Y from the symmetric GOE experiment, and divide by n>0. For probability laws the finite-measure mass correction in klDiv cancels; agreement with the displayed expectation needs absolute continuity and integrability of llr. klDiv is extended nonnegative and becomes infinity outside that branch, so converting toReal without finiteness would incorrectly erase infinity. The normalization is per latent row n, not n squared, and the latent variable is Lambda alone.

Use the law of (Lambda,A) under the asymmetric weak-signal experiment, marginalizing the independent Theta factor in the observation law. Compare to law(Lambda) times law(A) and normalize by n, retaining both prior parameters. Information between A and (Lambda,Theta) is a different quantity. As in D13, a finite real expectation requires the appropriate absolute-continuity and log-integrability proof; generic KL construction does not prove asymptotic equality with the symmetric model. Later theorems importing Theorem 4.3 conditions do not thereby import its information conclusion.

variant_reviews.comparison: Construct Y=sqrt(gamma)*Lambda0+G with independent G of law N(0,1), and identify its conditional density-ratio information with joint-versus-product KL only under the requisite probability and integrability conditions. For fixed s>0 retain Psi=s^2/4+gamma^2/(4s)-gamma/2+I(gamma). A candidate gamma>0 must satisfy IsMaxOn over (0,infinity), plus HasDerivAt with derivative zero and leastness among positive stationary points. IsMaxOn alone does not include domain membership; the totalized derivative being zero would also count nondifferentiable points, so use HasDerivAt. Since I(gamma)>=0, the positive quadratic forces unbounded growth as gamma tends to infinity and prevents a finite attained global maximum. No maximum-to-minimum or sign correction is inferred, and this remains only alternative (c), not a common assumption of every branch.

variant_reviews.comparison: Take the finite span of selected design columns in real n-space with empirical inner product equal to the Euclidean inner product divided by n>0. Positive uniform rescaling preserves orthogonality, so the Euclidean starProjection gives the same fitted n-vector. This exists even with dependent selected columns, unlike a plain Gram inverse. For full-column-rank A_k the column-span starProjection can be identified with A_k(A_k^T A_k)^(-1)A_k^T after proving the Gram matrix invertible. An orthonormal basis U_k of that span gives U_k U_k^T. Singular-vector selection is unnecessary for the invariant projection itself, and sign choices do not alter a fixed full loading span. Lower-bound theorems that bind their own orthonormal U and P=UU^T do not need the entire general data model merely to use this equality.

Use the finite span of the first k supplied orthonormal covariance eigenvectors, giving beta_prefix=sum_{i<=k} inner(beta,v_i)*v_i and beta_tail=beta-beta_prefix in the underlying Hilbert space. The same operator can act on theta in Theorem 3. The selected eigendecomposition controls any ties; no basis-free unique prefix is asserted at a tied boundary. Only the finite-prefix projection is needed, including in an infinite-dimensional setting, and the nearby proposition bounds are not extra assumptions of the definition.

Use the Frobenius inner product on the finite matrix-entry space. The subspace supported on Omega has projection given entrywise by the Omega indicator; its complement, the diagonal mask and off-diagonal complement are distinct specified operators. A general subset of matrix entries is not a column-space projection or matrix multiplication by a square projector. Do not substitute spectral norm geometry for this Euclidean/Frobenius least-squares construction.

In L2(F-star), assume the supplied correction basis functions and g are square integrable, form their finite span and project g; starProjection_minimal gives the least-squares meaning after relating squared distance to the displayed integral. Uniqueness is as an L2 equivalence class; a pointwise formula and unique coefficients require the relevant representative and nonsingular Gram assumptions. The population Omega interpretation comes from the source coordinate formula and must not be presented as a separately printed definition or estimated nuisance. Preserve the recorded F-star normalization ambiguity and use its actual supplied measure rather than silently normalize it.

For each superscript, form the column span of the named concatenated design, such as (Z_pi,Z) or (x,Z,Z_pi), and take its Euclidean starProjection. variant_reviews.comparison: Pi-prime is a Borel probability on divergence-free zero-mean fields in V intersect H2, and centering must be stated in addition to IsGaussian or IsGaussianProcess. A finite-marginal Gaussian process does not by itself give Borel sample paths in this Sobolev space. The RKHS must be the one associated with this Gaussian law, not an arbitrary RKHS instance, and completeness and a continuous injective embedding into V intersect H^alpha are additional requirements. Alpha>=2 may be fractional, beyond the source's earlier integer Sobolev definition. Push forward by theta-prime mapped to N^(-1/(2*alpha+2))*theta-prime for N>0. This is the prior scaling, not a claimed contraction rate; its base RKHS is distinct from PDE space H. RKHS regularity does not assert that typical prior draws lie in H^alpha or in the RKHS itself, and the following Fourier-series example is optional.

variant_reviews.comparison: Condition the real response y on the p-dimensional x with the stated joint support Y times X; preserve 'random sample' as source wording, and use square integrability for the stated mean-squared prediction optimality rather than inferring finite risk from mere existence of a conditional mean.
Use the observed-law conditional mean mu_0(l,a)=E[Y|L=l,A=a], conditioning jointly on covariates and treatment; it is not itself a potential-outcome estimand or a causal-identification result.
For each t=0,1 define r_t(x)=E[Y(t)|X=x] using the potential outcome as the response; no linearity, sparsity or identification with E[Y|T=t,X=x] follows without the source's separate assumptions.

The target is m(z)=E[Y|Z=z], while m-hat is a fitted nuisance function whose training data depend on the selected algorithm; the definition does not equate the fitted function with its target or with the full regression on (X,Z).

Under each n-dependent true law L_n, define both mu_n,x(Z)=E[X|Z] and mu_n,y(Z)=E[Y|Z], then evaluate their chosen versions at observed Z_i; fitted means are distinct data-dependent inputs and no regression algorithm or learned conditional law is prescribed here.
For each P use g_P(x,z)=E_P[Y|X=x,Z=z], retaining the full predictor block; equality with the response-on-Z function m_P is a conditional-mean null condition, not part of this definition.

Standard existence/uniqueness reasoning needs lambda>=0 and is not supplied by the IsMinOn predicate alone.

Specialize D to the displayed shrinking-row Kronecker matrix D_(n,d)^(k+1) and preserve the same one-half loss and unnormalized L1 penalty. The source calls this equivalent to the earlier fixed-length finite-difference problem, but its recorded boundary discrepancy means that equation (7)'s explicit matrix formulation must remain the definition used here. The KTF specialization adds the valid regular-lattice and difference-order domain; it does not change the general objective's norm conventions or assert its statistical risk bound by definition.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use q_(b0+eta) in U1 and q_(b0-eta) in U2, multiplying each localized kernel by the square root of its own density. Normalize the Gaussian integral by that weighted kernel's L2 norm and subtract Upsilon of its squared norm divided by the corresponding indicator-weighted L2 norm squared on [-A,A]. Both integrals use the same spatial W, not independent drivers or the observation-time noise; their cross-covariance depends on the two weighted kernels together. Take each supremum over the rational location-bandwidth set and then max(U1,U2). A zero kernel allowed in some inherited conditions makes Gaussian normalizers degenerate and is not resolved by a generic Gaussian-process predicate or a classical Bochner integral.

variant_reviews.comparison: For the one-group marginal density g(Y|psi), integrate the outer product of its log-density gradient, with entries indexed d,d'=1,...,D. The source omits the expectation subscript; the conventional law is g(.;psi), which must be specified rather than silently using the true-parameter law for every psi. Keep this marginal information distinct from the f-model information in the same paper's Bernstein-von Mises theorem. Derivatives, log-density domains and finite score moments are needed; positive definiteness is not a consequence of the formula alone.

Use the DQM score s_theta and expectation under P_theta to define I_theta(P)=E_theta[s_theta*s_theta^T]. DQM supplies the cited zero-score-mean and finite-information conclusions, which remain theorem-level implications rather than the body of Matrix.vecMulVec or integral. Do not require a pointwise log-density derivative where the DQM definition supplies only an L2 score, and do not impose positive definite information in cases where the source allows a singular matrix.

The max-with-one conventions retain the no-rejection and no-signal cases.

variant_reviews.comparison: For o_P(1), every epsilon>0 requires the supremum over the current class P_n of P_P(abs(X_Pn)>epsilon) to tend to zero. For O_P(1), every epsilon>0 admits M_epsilon,N_epsilon valid simultaneously for all n>=N_epsilon and all P in P_n, with the printed double supremum strictly below epsilon. For a random scale Y require the displayed multiplicative representation X=Y*R with R of the corresponding uniform order; at zeros of Y it forces X=0 and does not mean an arbitrary quotient with a zero fallback. variant_reviews.comparison: Choose common C>=1 and c in (0,1]. Clause (a) uses epsilon_P=Y-m_P(Z), so E[epsilon_P^2|X,Z]>=c is not the same as a lower conditional variance bound under alternatives; its higher moment is E[abs(epsilon_P)^(2+delta)|X,Z]<=C. The printed order is for each P there exists delta in (0,2], not one common delta before all P; the later theorem's single growth exponent remains a flagged uniformity issue. Clause (b) requires the joint X,Z law to have a density on the cube with the displayed pointwise supremum and infimum bounds; arbitrary almost-everywhere density versions need not meet those pointwise bounds. Clause (c) asks for z-smoothness of p_{X|Z,P}(x|dot) at each fixed x, uniformly over x, m_P smooth in dZ variables and g_P smooth in all d variables, all under one H_s bound with 0<s<=r. Generic HolderOnWith cannot settle the missing S24 norm or higher-derivative conventions. Do not reverse the conditional-density smoothness direction or add projection-residual assumptions.

Generic matrix operations do not supply that nondegeneracy condition.

variant_reviews.comparison: Require a real probability CDF F with F(-x)=1-F(x) for every x, so F(0)=1/2, and express F(x)-1/2-eta*x=O(x^2) along x tending to zero using IsBigO on the corresponding neighborhood or punctured-neighborhood filter. This is a deterministic local remainder, not stochastic order or merely little-o(x). The expansion identifies the derivative at zero as eta, and CDF monotonicity implies eta>=0, but the printed eta in Real does not exclude eta=0. Later polynomials dividing by eta therefore need an unresolved extra convention or restriction rather than a silent eta>0 assumption. The exact reflection equation is stronger than carelessly invoking symmetry with unspecified atom conventions. An admissible CDF may reach 0 or 1, so the source's later open-interval skewing-weight statement is not automatic, and no logistic or Gaussian CDF is selected by this generic definition.

variant_reviews.comparison: For a feasible e-statistic T take inf_g E_Qg[log T], then maximize this criterion over the entire e-statistic class. variant_reviews.comparison: Use prior.bind (fun theta => P_theta) after supplying measurability of the measure-valued family, or the corresponding Markov kernel construction. Its mass on measurable B is the integral of P_theta(B) against the probability prior. The superscript theta, or g in group-indexed applications, binds an integration variable and is neither exponentiation nor a group action on a measure. Theorem 1 permits separate priors for the null and alternative mixtures; no shared prior, Haar measure or mixture of likelihood ratios is inferred. A Haar measure on a noncompact group need not be a probability prior and is not silently substituted. The bare bind constructor has no intended probabilistic interpretation without its measurable-transition requirements.

variant_reviews.comparison: Keep both model families equivariant and dominated by one mu, with mu(gB)=chi(g)*mu(B) for every measurable B and g. variant_reviews.comparison: Ordinary invariance requires m(gx)=m(x) for all g,x. Maximal invariance further requires m(x)=m(x-prime) iff x lies in orbit G x-prime, exactly the relation used by orbitRel. Thus m factors through the orbit quotient and is injective on quotient classes, but need not be onto an arbitrarily chosen codomain. A quotient relation or an abstract representative choice does not automatically provide a measurable statistic or a convenient standard-Borel quotient. The group-action orientation in x=g*x-prime is retained; symmetry of the orbit relation is a consequence of the group laws. Theorem 1's arbitrary statistic V_n is not required to have this stronger property.

In a metrizable space second countability corresponds to the separability in the source description, and complete metrizability means existence of a compatible complete metric rather than completeness of every chosen metric. variant_reviews.comparison: For each fixed g first compute E_Qg[log T]-sup_{T-prime an e-statistic} E_Qg[log T-prime], then take inf over g, and maximize the resulting value over feasible T. The oracle may optimize separately for each g, but each candidate T-prime must still satisfy the full composite-null e-statistic constraint. Do not move the subtraction outside the infimum or use a common oracle optimizer without proof. Zero statistics require the extended logarithm and infinite oracle values can produce undefined differences unless additional conditions resolve them. Theorem 4 proves a constant oracle value and equivalence of optimizer sets under its assumptions; that result is neither this definition nor a proof of optimizer existence, and it does not import the other parts of Assumption 1.

variant_reviews.comparison: With Group G and MulAction G Z, isCancelSMul_iff_eq_one_of_smul_eq states IsCancelSMul G Z iff forall g,z, g acting on z=z implies g=1, exactly the printed trivial-stabilizer criterion. variant_reviews.comparison: Define tilde-beta+1=min(beta+1,d/2), then tilde-delta_n=n^(-1/(2*tilde-beta+d)), and D=F-hat^(tilde-beta+1,tilde-delta_n). variant_reviews.comparison: On the chosen integer interval I, minimize the unnormalized residual-square sum plus lambda sqrt(card I) times the sum of absolute coefficients, with lambda > 0. The L1 norm uses PiLp 1 or an explicit absolute-value sum, not the default function-space supremum norm. Multiplying the complete objective by one half matches the half-squared-error convention with effective penalty lambda sqrt(card I)/2; dividing by positive card I matches Algorithm 1. Such transformations retain the interval and require positive scaling. IsMinOn on all real coefficient vectors specifies optimality but does not choose a unique or measurable estimator. No stochastic regression assumptions are needed to state this data-based criterion.

The objective is one half the Euclidean residual norm squared plus lambda times the L1 coefficient norm, without a 1/n factor. Record the selected support as exactly the nonzero coordinates of the chosen beta-hat. The displayed source does not explicitly restrict lambda or settle ties among Lasso solutions, so neither a positive tuning assumption nor a canonical support is silently inserted. The checked primitives express the criterion and optimality relation; existence, uniqueness and measurable selection do not follow from IsMinOn alone.

For group j sum residual squares only over H_j and divide by 2 n_j, then add lambda times the L1 norm. With positive n_j, multiplying by n_j gives the half-squared-error convention with penalty n_j lambda, preserving the group's normalization. This is a local estimator, not a pooled fit over all groups. The formula alone does not guarantee uniqueness or provide a measurable choice, and division by a zero group size has no statistical meaning supplied by totalized field division.

variant_reviews.comparison: Preserve the descending l loop inside r=2,...,n+1, accumulating M by X_l X_l transpose and V by y_l X_l transpose for I=[l,r). On long intervals the objective is the fitted quadratic divided by card I plus lambda/sqrt(card I) times the L1 norm, consistent with dividing (14) by the positive interval length after dropping its coefficient-independent response squares. Short intervals receive zero G. B_1 starts at -zeta and the recurrence adds zeta; update only when b < B_r, retaining the earlier encountered candidate on a tie. The printed pointer vector has length n but can be assigned at r=n+1; backtracking starts at k=n and adds every predecessor h, potentially the boundary 1. V is initialized as a vector but used with a row orientation, and the output segment fits lack an explicit retention step. These frozen source issues prevent treating the literal pseudocode as an already well-defined verified implementation; no silent indexing repair is made.

variant_reviews.comparison: The algorithm uses beta-hat_k and beta-hat_{k+1} in both residual products, sums the two products into Z_t, sets S=floor((e_k-s_k)/(2R)), and constructs 2R consecutive blocks of width S, discarding any remainder. Each D_r is the difference of adjacent block sums divided by sqrt(2S), and the output is sum D_r squared divided by R times kappa-hat_k squared. R counts block pairs and is not their width. The input list ends at K-hat, leaving the last k+1 coefficient unsupplied; surrounding (17) and (30) instead use k-1 and k, and the source does not justify replacing the indices. Noninteger endpoints, R=0, S=0 and kappa-hat_k=0 also require explicit conventions or hypotheses. The subsequent prose's reciprocal floor identity is not substituted for the algorithm's S formula, and real totalized division does not supply a statistical fallback.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use gaussianReal 0 1 for each z_i^(b) and joint independence for the stated within-repetition Gaussian family. At r<0 sum from ceil(n r) through -1, at r>0 from 1 through floor(n r), divide both by sqrt(n), and set the value at zero to zero. No interpolation or sign reversal on the negative branch is added. Minimize varpi-hat_k abs r plus sigma-hat_infinity(k), the standard-deviation scale rather than the variance itself, times that step process over the open interval (-M,M). IsMinOn does not supply membership, attainment, uniqueness or measurable choice. Step 1 assumes finite M and a finite Gaussian index range, while Theorem 10 sets M to infinity and needs a countable extension; independence from data and a complete joint law across b are not separately specified. The presence of jumps and an open domain prevents automatically applying continuous compact minimum attainment.

variant_reviews.comparison: Given the data, use the empirical measure n^(-1) sum_{j=1}^n dirac X_j and take its n-fold finite product. Observations with the same value retain their index multiplicity in that sum; sampling is with replacement and conditionally iid. This is neither sampling original indices without replacement nor summing all bootstrap-position m-tuples. Positive n and n>=m are needed for the usual probability and combinatorial normalization.

variant_reviews.comparison: Require epsilon-tilde_n>=sqrt(log n/n) and epsilon-tilde_n tending to zero, positive c_1,...,c_4,K-prime and P_n contained in the signal laws whose induced observation law mu_Y has M_{4+delta}<=K-prime epsilon-tilde_n^(-2). The entropy is log D(epsilon-tilde_n,F(P_n),d)<=c_1 n epsilon-tilde_n^2 using the source's nonstrict packing and density identification. The outside prior mass bound is c_3 exp(-(c_2+4)n epsilon-tilde_n^2), while KL small-ball mass is at least c_4 exp(-c_2 n epsilon-tilde_n^2) around P_0Y, including the raw second log moment. The prior is specified on signal/mixing parameters, so the observation-law event uses its induced law. These are hypotheses of Theorem 4.1 and conclusions asserted by Theorems 4.2/4.4, not automatically inherited hypotheses in every later reference.

variant_reviews.comparison: All responses lie in a common Polish space with its Borel sigma-algebra and a common sigma-finite reference mu. WithDensity represents f_x or g_x after their nonnegativity, measurability and unit integrals are supplied. At time t the conditional response law depends only on X_t=x and L_t=i even when conditioning also on F_{t-1} and the preceding latent states; use f_x for i=0 and g_x for i=1. This conditional law does not make the unconditional responses independent or Gaussian, and it does not expose the latent states to the policy. Exact-state conditioning requires an appropriate version rather than interpreting an arbitrary null event literally.

variant_reviews.comparison: ConvexOn R univ g is the natural ambient convex-objective ingredient; using ConvexOn R Theta g would additionally demand convexity of the grouped/sparse domain and would strengthen the source. variant_reviews.comparison: The first oracle minimizes over parameters with exactly the same nonzero coordinate groups as beta-star, which requires fitted group values to be distinct and nonzero and true-zero coordinates to stay zero. The second minimizes without these level constraints over R^(K0+q), then assigns fitted gamma values back to each true class. Such fitted values may coincide or equal zero, violating the first constraint; full column rank alone would not prevent that. IsMinOn with separate membership represents either formulation but does not identify them, choose a unique solution, or ensure attainment on the group-equality set. Preserve the source discrepancy rather than adding rank or nonzero-fit assumptions.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use a probability measure P0_n and a family Ptheta_n indexed by theta in the specified subset of R^d on the data space for each n. Both are absolutely continuous with respect to the same sigma-finite mu_n; the finite laws have the decomposition needed by rnDeriv, and withDensity reconstructs them once the singular part vanishes. Domination by mu_n does not imply P0_n is absolutely continuous with respect to every Ptheta_n. The density is a version, and joint measurability in theta is an additional requirement for a kernel construction, not a consequence of the family notation. No product/iid law or theta with Ptheta_n = P0_n is imposed.

variant_reviews.comparison: The likelihood is log of the chosen model density ptheta_n at observed X^n, with no iid factorization and no equality to the true density. Real.log agrees on positive finite inputs but log 0 = 0 would misrepresent a zero likelihood; ENNReal.log can represent negative infinity there and positive infinity at an infinite density. A derivative-based real objective needs the corresponding local positive finite density domain and compatible version. The common dominating measure alone does not certify these pointwise conditions uniformly in theta.

Retain -n/2 log(2 pi), -1/2 log(det V), and -1/2 times the residual transpose V-inverse residual, with residual y-X xi. Vertical bars mean determinant, not a matrix norm or an instruction to take abs(det V). Matrix inverse identities require nonsingularity; a Gaussian Lebesgue-density interpretation needs positive-definite covariance, and the archived source review leaves the full Omega domain unspecified. Real.log of a negative determinant and the zero inverse of a singular matrix are not valid replacements for that missing domain. This is the working Gaussian objective even when the true random effects are non-Gaussian; it does not supply Gaussian information equality or the later adjusted-likelihood score signs.

variant_reviews.comparison: The first event simultaneously bounds the minimum eigenvalue of Omega-hat-inverse strictly above eta-bar1 and the maximum strictly below eta-bar2, with probability >1-epsilon-hat-n,1. eigenvalues-zero are sorted real eigenvalues only for a Hermitian matrix and need positive dimension for extrema. The second event is a separate intersection of three strict supremum bounds on B_delta(theta-hat) = Theta intersect the open Euclidean ball around the random MAP: the unscaled log-prior Hessian, likelihood third derivative divided by n, and likelihood fourth derivative divided by n. Constants delta,L_pi2,L3,L4 are fixed positive numbers; its probability error epsilon-hat-n,2 tends to zero separately. The source names spectral norms for higher tensors without specifying whether diagonal or independent-unit-vector contraction is intended, so the ordinary continuous-multilinear operator norm cannot be asserted equal without review. No fixed center theta-star, shrinking radius, deterministic global derivative bound or independent-event product replaces the stated conditions.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use Omega-hat = inverse(J(theta-hat)/n), then its CC, complement-complement and cross blocks; Lambda_C = Omega_complement,C times inverse(Omega_CC), and barOmega subtracts Omega_complement,C inverse(Omega_CC) Omega_C,complement from Omega_complement,complement. The conditional mean is Lambda_C h-hat_C and covariance barOmega. The left quadratic exponent has Einstein sums over s,t and factor 1/(2n); its proportionality omits the Gaussian normalizer, while the displayed density product is an equality. A valid nondegenerate Gaussian density needs positive-definite full covariance and corresponding invertible blocks; multivariateGaussian's Dirac fallback on a non-PSD matrix or a singular measure is not that density. No complement-of-high-probability-event fallback is supplied by the paper, and empty/full C cases need separate zero-dimensional conventions. This MAP likelihood covariance is distinct from the theoretical covariance in the general theorem and from a full posterior Hessian inverse.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use RKHS R H X R together with CompleteSpace H; the class itself only supplies the continuous injective function map, so completeness cannot be omitted. For v=1, kerFun_inner gives inner(kerFun H x 1,f)=f(x), and the kernel identity identifies kerFun H x 1 with K(.,x)=Phi_x. The construction and uniqueness apply to the supplied real symmetric PSD kernel after scalar-operator identification. The norm is H's own Hilbert norm; its completeness does not imply that its image is closed in L2(mu), so the later L2 projection issue remains separate.

Apply the complete scalar RKHS construction separately to kappa_U on Omega_U and kappa_Theta on Omega_Theta. The generated kernel equality and evaluation identity give the two spaces and their feature sections, without mixing their domains. Characteristicness, kernel measurability and embedding integrability, C2 regularity, boundedness and feature-Lipschitz conditions are distinct assumptions used by different theorems; none follows just from being an RKHS. The completed tensor product and Hilbert-Schmidt identification in D3 require a separate comparison.

Construct the complete real RKHS of covariance kernel K and define B_K as its norm-closed unit ball. RKHS.equiv gives uniqueness up to linear isometry for identical kernels, with the adjacent coe_equiv preserving functions; this is the appropriate interpretation rather than definitional equality of arbitrary Lean carrier types. The standing separability condition belongs to the dual-space passage and is not automatic for every kernel. The norm and inner product are those of H_K, not the residual-weighted L2(mu) geometry used in the projected-kernel spectral expansion.

variant_reviews.comparison: The space is L2 of the covariate law P_X. The p coordinate functions g span a finite-dimensional subspace; project onto its orthogonal complement and include the result back into L2. With square-integrable scores and nonsingular Gamma=E[g g-transpose], the coefficients of the removed projection are G(a,theta0) Gamma-inverse, with G=E[a g-transpose]. The inverse theorem needs nonzero determinant and supplies no generalized inverse. An L2 element is an equivalence class, so the pointwise formula chooses versions rather than a value intrinsic to the class. Neither the H_K norm nor the residual-weighted L2(mu) norm can replace P_X geometry here.

variant_reviews.comparison: The operator integrates K-perp(x1,x2) f(x1) against residual-second-moment weighted mu and returns an L2(mu) class. Boundedness, well-defined representatives, compactness and self-adjointness must precede use of the library spectral theorem; that theorem alone does not prove trace class or a summable sequence of nonnegative eigenvalues. Eigenfunctions here are orthonormal in L2(mu), not H_K. The source expansion is in L2(mu times mu) and separately asserted almost everywhere, so neither uniform pointwise convergence nor pointwise evaluation of arbitrary L2 classes is available automatically. Zero eigenvalues and their later RKHS representatives remain implicit, and the lambda normalization cannot be borrowed from the H_K covariance spectrum.

variant_reviews.comparison: The empirical law supplies both the outer average and the mean/covariance used in U-hat and Theta-hat, so all transformed sample terms depend on the same original data and are not iid transformed observations with known population parameters. The angular reference expectation remains E0 and is not fitted from the sample. Finite averaging preserves multiplicity and n^-1 normalization, and bilinearity yields the centered-feature formula. Invertibility of the sample covariance, positive radii and regular polar-coordinate conventions are required where these transforms are used; no ridge or pseudoinverse rule is printed. This is distinct from the known-parameter expression (7.1) with its different last expectation.

Both the transforms U(x,F),Theta(x,F) and the outer law dF vary with F, while P0 is held fixed. A single fixed integrand with only a changing measure would miss the location/scatter effect. The completed tensor Bochner expectation agrees with the centered expression under the required integrability and bilinear interchange conditions. The object is the discrepancy operator, not its squared norm. Identifying its empirical specialization requires the empirical moment convention used by the source and valid sample inverse/chart domains; it does not establish Frechet differentiability or a delta-method conclusion.

variant_reviews.comparison: Probability distributions alone form no vector space containing F-F0, so the printed linear A:F->H cannot be interpreted literally as a linear map on that carrier. One needs an ambient space of signed directions or an equivalent distribution-function representation, a specified multivariate uniform metric/norm and an appropriate bounded linear extension A. HasFDerivWithinAt then expresses the small remainder as F approaches F0 through valid distributions, while IsLittleO compares remainder and perturbation norms. A total-variation signed-measure norm would be a different topology and cannot be silently substituted. This is the explicit regularity assumption in Theorem2, not a consequence of contamination derivatives or an unprinted assumption added to Theorem3.

variant_reviews.comparison: The direct contamination term is radial feature at U(z) tensor reference-centered angular feature at Theta(z), followed by minus the population Sigma_UTheta. The first expectation differentiates the radial feature and multiplies U-star(X,z); the second differentiates the angular feature and contracts with Theta-star(X,z). Both account for estimating moments from F, while P0 is fixed and has no derivative. Keep the negative population term away from H0 and do not substitute a later empirically centered estimate. Bochner integrability, feature derivatives and differentiation/interchange conditions are needed for the calculation; the assumed Frechet regularity does not make totalized integrals or exceptional polar coordinates valid. This is the operator influence, not the derivative of its squared Hilbert-Schmidt norm.

Positivity of their product and n, a nonempty E, and finite measurable coefficients are needed for the intended finite conditional law. An appropriate alpha domain makes the quantile set nonempty and bounded below; real sInf outside those conditions is not a justified quantile.
