Equation (6.1) uses the same conditional generalized-quantile expression but refers to some multiplier statistic without giving its concrete construction. Its target is the CENTERED T_E=max_e sqrt(n)|tilde-Theta_e-Theta_e|, distinct from (2.2). The precision-model formula is not inherited merely because the quantile names agree. Assumption 6.1 gives approximation requirements against T_0E^B, not equality of the unspecified actual statistic with that ideal statistic. Conditional probability can be the multiplier law for each fixed dataset, subject to measurability for subsequent outer probabilities; generic CDF and infimum ingredients do not prove bootstrap validity.

variant_reviews.comparison: Theta maps d2 predictor coordinates to d1 responses, and Y_i=Theta X_i+E_i. A diagonal Gaussian covariance supports coordinate independence only after the relevant joint Gaussian law is established; merely assigning individual Gaussian marginals does not do so. The independent-noise model and conditional formulation must be connected by a proof, not silently inferred from iid pairs alone. Matrix primitives preserve the rectangular dimensions and shared-design orientation; no graphical precision model is substituted.

variant_reviews.comparison: For response indices [d1], H0 consists of rows with fewer than k_tau nonzero coordinates and d0 is its cardinality. B filters its complement by the requirement that EVERY nonzero entry exceed c sqrt(log d2/n) in absolute value, strictly. This is stronger than having merely k_tau strong entries or a large largest entry. rho=|B|/d1 is the fraction of all response rows, not the fraction within H0-complement. Support is exact nonzero support and the complement is relative to the finite response index domain; d1>0 and n>0 are needed for the intended normalization and rate.

The square version uses row indices [d], threshold c sqrt(log d/n) and rho=|B|/d. The printed H0 uses the entire row norm including its diagonal, whereas Section 2.1's graph-degree vector excludes that diagonal. Preserve both original conventions rather than removing a nonzero precision diagonal here. Again every nonzero coordinate must pass the strict threshold and the denominator counts all nodes. Section 6 reuses d0 and rho from this occurrence without inheriting Gaussian observation assumptions. Finite filtering/cardinality supplies the set arithmetic but does not resolve the source's degree/full-row discrepancy.

variant_reviews.comparison: K=floor(N^(1/d))^2 floor(L^(1/d))^2 for positive integer N,L and positive dimension, and alpha ranges over {1,...,K}^d. Q_alpha(Delta) uses closed coordinate intervals [(alpha_i-1)/K,alpha_i/K-1_{alpha_i<K} Delta] for every coordinate. Set.pi of Set.Icc expresses those simultaneous inequalities, with the all-coordinate interpretation recorded separately from the source display's abbreviated quantifier. The final coordinate cell has no subtraction and reaches 1; this is not a half-open partition and the nonterminal cells have one-sided gaps. Delta lies in (0,1/(3K)] and epsilon in (0,1); the precision parameter and arbitrary y_alpha in [0,1] do not alter Q. Real roots and floors require positive-domain typing and a justified positive natural K. No global bound on the fitted network away from these regions follows from this set definition.

variant_reviews.comparison: The definition selects f0,tau in argmin over Theta of R_tau, so membership in the measurable bounded class must accompany IsMinOn. It is not minimization over the network class or the empirical sample. Finite positive tau gives a loss with linear tails, allowing finite risk under the first-moment setting and bounded functions once proved. At tau=infinity the loss is half squared error, and finite first moment alone does not give finite population risk; a real integral's nonintegrable zero fallback cannot stand for infinite loss. An extended-risk formulation or the appropriate second-moment domain is required there. Mean-zero asymmetric noise can shift the Huber minimizer away from f0; uniqueness, measurable selection and representative choices are not established by IsMinOn. The later empirical comparison to f0,tau makes those representative choices material.

variant_reviews.comparison: Candidates belong to F_n(d,L-bar,N-bar,1). The first branch requires empirical risk at most min{empirical risk of f0,tau, inf over that network class of empirical risk+c9 delta^2}; this is BOTH comparisons, not a choice between them. The second branch is OR empirical risk at most the same infimum+n^-100. Preserve this union and the arbitrary robustification parameter rather than replacing it with the upper-bound set S_n,tau(delta). c9 is universal and independent of architecture, n and tau. Infimum order facts require a nonempty class and a lower-bounded real objective range, obtainable for valid finite sample losses and an established zero network; they do not assume exact minimizer attainment. Population f0,tau need not be a member of the network class. Huber at infinity has the source's half-squared-loss normalization, so numeric tolerances cannot be transferred unchanged to (2.3). The lower theorem asserts existence of a bad eligible estimator, not that every eligible member is bad.

variant_reviews.comparison: For every x in the cube the conditional law of epsilon given X=x is symmetric about zero and its integral of |epsilon| is at most v1>0. At a fixed conditional law, IdentDistrib of the identity and negation expresses symmetry once their measurability is established. condDistrib supplies a regular conditional kernel for real noise, but the connection to conditioning and uniqueness is almost everywhere in X; it does not certify these every-x properties of an arbitrary version. A version satisfying them must be stipulated or constructed, including values at null covariates. Finite absolute first moments justify actual integrals and conditional means; nonintegrable zero fallback is not a bound. Neither finite variance nor independence of the conditional law from x follows, and Theorem 3.7's separate c1 parameter-scope issue cannot be resolved by silently imposing Condition 2 at order two.

variant_reviews.comparison: F_l is the conditional CDF of epsilon given Z on machine l, and epsilon is independent of X conditional on Z. CondIndepFun uses the sigma-algebra generated by measurable Z and the corresponding finite machine law; its standard-Borel ambient-space requirements must be met. For each k=1,...,alpha+1 a positive M_F,k bounds sup over epsilon AND l of |F_l^(k)(epsilon|Z)| for almost every Z in the source's machine-law interpretation. Ordinary iteratedDeriv is totalized and therefore requires separate derivative-existence witnesses; a bound on its default values is not smoothness. Conditional kernels give laws only up to null-set versions, so version and almost-everywhere statements must be coordinated across machines. Median zero means the two median tail inequalities; with the imposed continuity it can be related to F_l(0)=1/2, but median is not replaced by mean zero. No single shared F is imposed.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each machine define zeta=X+Z^T beta-star and represent its conditional law given Z by rho_l against real Lebesgue measure. withDensity needs a nonnegative density representation and normalization to make a probability law; simply constructing a weighted measure does not prove it equals the conditional kernel. For almost every Z the source requires rho_l positive and uniformly bounded, and for each k=1,...,alpha explicitly bounds sup over zeta,l of |rho_l^(k)(zeta|Z)| by a common positive M_rho,k. Preserve the exact zeroth-order wording rather than inferring a numerical positive lower bound or importing the homogeneous assumption's wording. Derivatives need actual existence, not totalized iteratedDeriv values. The smooth positive density is a chosen version; arbitrary almost-everywhere modifications of a Radon-Nikodym derivative need not retain those pointwise properties.

variant_reviews.comparison: At the current beta, form A=sum_l W_l nabla^2 F_h,l(beta) and b=sum_l W_l nabla F_h,l(beta), then update beta to beta-A^-1 b. The inverse identity requires a unit determinant, not merely the Assumption 9 norm bounds and sum W_l=I. The preceding sum W_l F_h,l(beta) is matrix-valued because F_h,l is scalar, so no usual scalar argmin or potential-function gradient is supplied by that prose. variant_reviews.comparison: For positive k, use n independent uniform labels in [k], then the deterministic map to M with within-label p and between-label q, symmetrically off diagonal and zero on the diagonal. The finite map is measurable, which is needed for Measure.map to represent its actual pushforward rather than its nonmeasurable fallback. Label counts are random, can be zero and are not conditioned on balance. The resulting prior is not generally uniform on distinct matrices or unlabelled partitions because preimage multiplicities can differ. The prior is a law on M; the risk experiment also samples conditionally independent Bernoulli edges from M. The auxiliary randomness of Algorithm 1 is a further layer, not already integrated merely by naming this signal prior.

variant_reviews.comparison: On D={(x,y) in [0,1]^2:x>=y}, sum two terms: max over j+k<=floor(gamma) of sup_D |partial_x^j partial_y^k f|, plus max over j+k=floor(gamma) of the off-diagonal difference-quotient supremum with denominator (|x-x'|+|y-y'|)^(gamma-floor(gamma)). The first term is E phi_(ell,j),1 times E phi_(i,j),0 divided by mu_ell,1; the second switches 0/1 and divides by mu_ell,2, with a PLUS sign. b_ell=(p-1)^-1 sum_i!=ell lambda_i,ell^2 Var(Z_i,ell). b-tilde_ell uses 1/(2N), N=(p-1)(p-2), times ((mu1+mu2)/(mu1 mu2))^2 and the sum over ORDERED distinct i,j avoiding ell of Var(Z_i,ell) Var(Z_ell,j) Var(Z_i,j). Average the three dagger factors over H_ell={(i,j):i,j!=ell,i<j}, using edge types (1,0,1) for mu1-hat-dagger and (0,1,0) for mu2-hat-dagger. Then theta-hat-ell-dagger is one-half log of their ratio. Theorem 2 centers at original theta and uses unconditional population scaling, not a conditional bootstrap law centered at theta-hat.

For active ell, xi=-omega1 log p+xi-plus and check-theta_ell=omega2 log p+check-theta_ell-plus, where omega1 in [0,2), omega2 in [0,1), 0<=omega1-omega2<1 and the absolute residuals are o(log p). Signed residuals are allowed. Empty S is not excluded but leaves the displayed maximum without a convention. theta_ell=xi/2+check-theta_ell applies also to inactive nodes; the later source norm assertion omitting their xi/2 terms is not imported. Theorem 4 imposes further omega restrictions separately.

xi-hat=(2/p) sum_ell theta-hat_ell and check-theta-hat_ell=theta-hat_ell-xi-hat/2. At the population parameter, twice the mean theta is xi+(2/p)sum_ell check-theta_ell, so this is not an exact inverse of the sparse normalization min check-theta=0. Sparse-rate assumptions must control that contamination bias; s=o(p) alone does not bound arbitrarily growing active effects. These estimates are unthresholded, can be negative and need not have support S; no support recovery or projection to the nonnegative cone is part of the formula. They inherit the original log-ratio estimator's finite-sample domain issue. Theorem 4's printed equality chain between different random errors remains a source qualification rather than an algebraic identity of these estimators.

variant_reviews.comparison: Asymptotic linearity is theta-hat=theta-star+n^-1 sum_i IF(O_i)+o_p(n^-1/2), with IF in L0^2(P-star), meaning a genuine finite second moment and zero mean. Since a is numerically 0 or 1, 1-a equals the target indicator; this is not valid as a multi-source indicator formula without modification. At true rho and r, DS.1 allows the target and mixture E(X) means to cancel when integrable, but mean zero alone does not establish efficiency. Finite target loss variance and suitable L2 nuisance control are needed for an influence-function interpretation, while the efficient branch uses the true conditional risk and statistical regularity. The prefix law under Q is absolutely continuous WITH RESPECT TO the prefix law under P-star conditioned on A in S-prime_k; the domination is not reversed and is weaker than bounded two-sided density ratios. For each a in that set, the conditional law of Z_k given the history and A=a equals its conditional law under Q for Q-almost every target history in Z_(k-1). Nonempty sets alone do not ensure positive conditioning mass for the pooled event or every individual a, so the source's conditional-law existence qualifications remain. Theorem 1 adds DS.0 only in its final drift-zero branch; the earlier drift-corrected expansion must not acquire it globally.

variant_reviews.comparison: Retain all eleven nu terms: tr(R D1); the n(n-1)/(4(n-2)^3) tr(D0 D1) correction; the positive n(2n-1)/((n-2)^2(n-2+p)) bracket; the negative tr(R D1)/(1+y_(n-2)) bracket with all five sample-size/kurtosis summands; the positive R D1 R trace and R^-1/2 entry correction; the positive tr(R D1)[2p+beta_w cubic-entry sum] term; its distinct negative 3n(n-1) fourth-entry-power correction; the negative 5n(n-1) bracket with diagonal R D1; and the three separate g-weighted double sums with R^-1 and R D1 R, with tr(R D1) R^-1 and R, and with D1 and R, respectively. Keep each denominator and the final 3n-6+p factor literally as archived. For sigma^2 retain the first three terms sharing ((1+2y)/(1-y))^2, including their positive quadratic forms and negative cross term, followed by five terms with (1+y)^-2: squared normalized trace times (2-2y-beta_w y), 2y times n^-1 tr(R D1)^2, squared normalized trace times [2n^-1 tr(R^2)+beta_w y], the negative product involving tr(R^2 D1), and the final diagonal-weighted sum. In particular tr[(R D1)^2], tr(R D1)^2 and [n^-1 tr(R D1)]^2 have different matrix/scalar powers and n factors. nu uses finite y_(n-2), while sigma^2 uses limiting y; no substitution is implicit. Fractional matrix powers need positive-definite population R, the contrast uses a genuine B inverse, n>2 is required, and y=1 makes the printed variance formula singular despite not being explicitly excluded by the preceding finite-y hypothesis. A zero contrast gives zero scale despite the source's arbitrary-contrast wording. Generic scalar totalization or cancellations do not establish a valid positive CLT normalizer or justify dropping terms.

variant_reviews.comparison: Z is the LOCATION attaining the maximum of W(t)-t^2 over all real t, not the maximum value or the argmax of a differently scaled drift. IsBrownianReal is indexed by nonnegative real time; a two-sided standard process needs compatible independent positive and negative Brownian halves joined at zero, not the same path reflected on both sides. IsMaxOn describes a maximizing point but gives no global attainment on the noncompact real line, a.s. uniqueness or measurable selection. Those require Brownian growth and argmax results beyond the inspected primitives. Measure.map gives the law only for an a.e.-measurable location map; its fallback must not hide a failed selection. The source's approximately 0.26 variance is a quoted property of this normalization and is not certified numerically by these declarations. Library Chernoff exponential tail bounds concern a different object.

Finset.image with classical equality on measures deduplicates equal restricted laws, and Finset.card counts exactly those distinct images. Set a_e to card image(H_Psi,e, restriction to s'_e), b_e to card image(G_Psi,e, restriction to s'_e), c_e to card image(H0, restriction to s_e), and d_e to card image(G_Psi,e, restriction to s_e). Projection may merge global laws, so neither cardinality of the global family nor a count of streams/units is interchangeable. Here restriction is to a subsystem sigma-field, equivalently the law of the subsystem process, not conditioning or measure restriction to an event. Empty images have cardinality zero without adding a positivity convention. These are coefficients for thresholds, not the numerical thresholds themselves.

variant_reviews.comparison: Use n measurable observations valued in [0,1]^d times a two-point treatment type times the reals, with iIndepFun across observations and IdentDistrib for their common joint law. These predicates concern whole triples and do not require X, A and Y within one observation to be independent. The source's blackboard P is the true joint law; a generic model law P and the covariate distribution F are distinct. F is obtained by measurable projection to X using Measure.map, with its multivariate distribution function defined from lower coordinate rectangles. A covariate density is needed only where asserted and requires absolute continuity; bounded covariate support alone provides neither such a density, positivity near x0, treatment overlap nor outcome moments. The totalized map branch for nonmeasurable functions is not an observation-law construction.

variant_reviews.comparison: For positive s let r be the largest integer strictly below s: at integer s, r=s-1 and the residual exponent is one, rather than taking an order-s derivative with exponent zero. ContDiffOn at finite order r gives the continuous differentiability component, while iteratedFDerivWithin evaluated on coordinate directions can represent the multi-index partial derivatives after the required within-domain uniqueness and coordinate identifications are proved. Bound every derivative of order at most r, including g itself at order zero, by the common finite C, and apply HolderOnWith exponent s-r to every order-r partial derivative. Use the Euclidean metric specified in the paper; the default supremum norm on a raw coordinate function space is not literally that norm. The multi-indices alpha and beta here are not the scalar nuisance smoothness indices. The omitted Holder radius stays fixed independently of n; the declarations alone provide neither its value nor a uniform bound across unrestricted functions.

variant_reviews.comparison: For d>0, take ambient Euclidean Haar measure, apply Measure.toSphere, and divide by its finite positive total mass to obtain the uniform sphere probability; raw toSphere is surface measure with mass d times the unit-ball volume, not already a probability. iIndepFun gives independent rows, as expressly recorded in Section 6, and IndepFun separates the row collection from the complete data sample. This definition admits a general activation; shifted ReLU is a later specialization. Training only theta does not resample W or fit its rows.

variant_reviews.comparison: Set H=W W transpose and M=E[1(Wx>0)1(Wx>0) transpose] with the expectation only over the standard Gaussian covariate and W fixed. Matrix.hadamard produces H entrywise-multiplied by M; the moment is a second moment, not a centered covariance. The unit row norms put each H_lk in [-1,1], and the displayed M_lk=(pi-arccos(H_lk))/(2*pi) is an entrywise Gaussian sign-probability identity, including correlation endpoints, rather than a matrix functional calculus arccos. After proving positive semidefiniteness, CFC.rpow at exponent 1/2 on the real matrix star algebra provides the operator square-root construction for J. This outer square root is spectral, not entrywise. Singular positive semidefinite matrices are allowed and no inverse or strict positivity is required. The intended squared norm identity is theta transpose J^2 theta; none of the inspected definitions proves the orthant formula or that identity from eta_i.

variant_reviews.comparison: For nonnegative epsilon_test in finite-dimensional Euclidean space, the closed perturbation ball is nonempty and compact. The shifted-ReLU squared residual is continuous in delta, so IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn supplies an attained maximum for each test pair and fixed theta,W. It does not establish maximum attainment for arbitrary f and arbitrary nonnegative loss, which are the general definition's only stated inputs, nor does it alone give a measurable selector or measurable maximum value. The expectation is outside the pointwise maximum and averages only over the test pair; it is not maximum of expected loss, and it does not average training or W randomness. Real integral needs finite integrable loss; lintegral can retain infinite nonnegative risk. Keep epsilon_test distinct from the training epsilon.

variant_reviews.comparison: With Matrix.Norms.L2Operator active, Matrix.l2_opNorm_def gives the correct norm of rectangular W:R^d to R^N. Require it at most sqrt(N/d)+C, and for every distinct row pair l,k require abs(inner(w_l,w_k)) at most log(d)/sqrt(d). Use Euclidean row inner products and positive d; the threshold is not a Frobenius norm bound and no factor of N is inserted. The source calls C sufficiently large but does not specify a numerical value. Diagonal row pairs are excluded, so this is an approximate off-diagonal orthogonality event, not exact orthogonality or a bound on the full Gram error by the same scalar. Defining the event does not establish its high-probability occurrence. The finite ratio N/d does not require signal normalization or a particular limiting ratio to write the event.

variant_reviews.comparison: For n>0 and nonnegative epsilon, maximize the 1/(2n) sum of squared residuals over one delta_i in the Euclidean epsilon-ball for each sample; these are separate coordinates of a finite compact product, not one shared perturbation. For fixed theta,W the objective is continuous in this tuple, so the inspected compact maximum theorem applies after assembling that product. Its value can be described as the sum of the separate maxima because the constraints separate, but that identity still needs proof. IsMinOn over all theta in R^N expresses outer optimality, not existence, uniqueness or a tie-selection rule; compactness of the inner perturbation domain does not make the unbounded coefficient domain compact. Keep W fixed and add no ridge penalty. The training radius epsilon is distinct from epsilon_test, and the objective's factor 1/(2n) is retained even though positive rescaling leaves its minimizers unchanged.

variant_reviews.comparison: Under gaussianReal 0 1, constant one and the identity function form an orthonormal pair in L2. For a square-integrable activation their projection coefficients are mu0=E sigma(G) and mu1=E G*sigma(G); the residual's squared norm is E sigma(G)^2-mu0^2-mu1^2, with the square root covering the entire difference. After proving this quantity nonnegative, Real.sqrt defines mu2 and the residual can be divided by mu2 when positive to define sigma_perp. Generic affine activations can have mu2=0, and the printed decomposition supplies no unique residual normalization there. For the specified shifted ReLU retain mu0=0, mu1=1/2 and mu2=sqrt(1/4-1/(2*pi)), whose explicit moment evaluations are not provided by the inspected primitives. Its full variance is 1/2-1/(2*pi), not one; the source's adjacent unit-variance assertion is not used to standardize sigma. Orthogonality here means the two stated Gaussian expectations vanish, not independence of residual features at different rows.

variant_reviews.comparison: Matrix.mulVec expresses A*Y=epsilon in the stated direction: A maps observations to latent components. Require A invertible, or its determinant a nonzero real, for the inverse reconstruction Y=A^-1 epsilon; the totalized matrix inverse alone does not assert this. Unit covariance is an additional hypothesis of the statistical identification statements and is not silently added to this initial model. Left multiplication by a later ambiguity matrix acts on A's rows.

variant_reviews.comparison: For even r>=2, write r=2*l+2 and sum over every l-tuple of labels in [d], repeating each chosen label twice and appending j,j. Finset.sum_apply justifies evaluating this finite sum of coordinate functions at j as the displayed sum of T entries. Require c_j(T) not equal c_k(T) for all j not equal k. Repetitions among the summation labels are allowed; these are not injective tuples or unordered combinations, and no combinatorial multiplicity factor is added. At l=0 the indexing function type has one empty tuple, so the contraction is T_jj, not an empty sum equal to zero. At higher order it involves mixed paired entries and is not merely distinct full diagonal entries. The differences c_j-c_k are linear in T, explaining the excluded hyperplanes once that linearity is proved. For a normalized statistical second-order moment/cumulant tensor the matrix is identity, so the distinctness condition fails when d>1; the source's algebraic condition is retained rather than silently removing r=2.

variant_reviews.comparison: Begin with the constant E eta(X)-1/2=P(Y=1)-1/2. For each nonzero pattern, condition the entire residual eta(X)-1/2-sum over all strict predecessors f_omega'(X) on the sigma-algebra generated by X^omega. Conditional expectation is defined for integrable residuals on the valid sub-sigma-algebra, and measurable factorization yields a function of the masked covariate when its hypotheses are met. The strict order is well founded by increasing Hamming weight, and all predecessors, not just immediate ones, occur in the subtraction. The recursion uses the unconditional test-pair law P rather than a law conditioned on O. Conditional expectations supply almost-everywhere identities; the displayed reconstruction as chosen functions needs compatible versions and cannot be obtained by treating arbitrary values on null fibers as canonical. No coordinate independence is assumed, and no alternate Hoeffding decomposition or orthogonality theorem from the excluded supplementary Proposition S3 is imported.

variant_reviews.comparison: For fixed x, form the real ratios nu.real(B_r(x))/r^s for 0<r<1 and s in [0,d]. This set is nonempty and bounded below by zero, so csInf_le and le_csInf_iff give a genuine infimum without an attaining radius. Each denominator is positive. The claimed upper bound one follows by considering radii approaching one and the probability bound, not by inserting the excluded radius r=1 or claiming every ratio is at most one. Open Euclidean balls must be retained. The exponent can be less than ambient d, as for a zero-filled pattern distribution; no Lebesgue density or positive uniform lower bound is assumed. Real measure evaluation is faithful because nu is a probability. An uncountable infimum of measurable functions is not automatically measurable, so the later event use needs a specific lower-density measurability argument rather than a generic infimum shortcut.

Both factors are in [0,1], so a measurable eta and classifier give a finite nonnegative integral. At eta=1/2 the Bayes rule chooses one but the contribution is zero even for disagreement. The result remains random through training data, and the theorem's subsequent conditional expectation over training given masks is outside this definition. No conditional training-feature measure replaces mu.

variant_reviews.comparison: Initialize f-hat_zero by the full label average minus 1/2. In ascending Hamming dimension, process every available nonzero pattern, use the literal k=1+floor(n_omega^[2 beta_omega gamma_omega/D]) and tau=2^-4*n_omega^[-beta_omega gamma_omega/(2D)] with D=gamma_omega(2 beta_omega+d_omega)+alpha beta_omega, and collect sample indices whose masks contain omega. Reorder neighbors by the printed masked Euclidean distances, average the first k labels, subtract 1/2 and every strict-predecessor estimate, then compute the average of squared fitted components over available cases. Finset.sort can order sample indices only after a total antisymmetric tie rule is chosen; distance alone permits ties, and duplicate feature values must not erase distinct sample indices. Function.update can store successive component values, but does not fill omitted evaluations: the loop lists X_i^(o_i) whereas the signal calculation uses X_i^omega, and the reordering statement mixes original-mask pairs with omega projections and retains its subscript defect. No cap is printed; n_omega=1 gives k=2 when the exponent is defined. If gamma_omega=alpha=0 the exponent is 0/0. These are not repaired by library totalization. In descending dimension, start selected Omega empty and use literally U({omega}) intersect selected Omega empty together with signal>=tau; because U includes incomparable patterns, this differs from predecessor-only prose and can make equal-dimension traversal order consequential. Finally reconstruct 1/2 plus the sum over selected Omega union its strict lower closure and output one at equality to 1/2. If selected Omega is empty, that reconstruction omits the estimated constant component as printed. The primitives establish neither a unique total algorithm nor the risk guarantee, and no unstated capping, tie breaking, clipping or source correction is inserted.

variant_reviews.comparison: For nonempty Q in Euclidean space, Metric.infDist is the infimum of norm(y-x). On an empty set its toReal-based definition returns zero rather than an extended infinite distance, so the source's unspecified empty-set case must not be silently identified with that value. The projection is the set of y in Q satisfying IsMinOn of distance; membership must be included because IsMinOn alone does not require it. Closed nonempty Euclidean sets attain the infimum by IsClosed.exists_infDist_eq_dist, but their projection can contain multiple points. Tangent spaces are finite-dimensional linear subspaces with a unique orthogonalProjectionOnto. Projection onto the nonlinear embedded manifold is a different, locally single-valued object under the regularity/neighborhood hypotheses used later; it is not a global orthogonal linear projection.

variant_reviews.comparison: The source requires, at each point of M, an open ambient U and a C^p map from U to some R^n with surjective Jacobian at that point and M intersect U equal to its zero fiber. ContDiffOn and fderiv express the local regularity and derivative once the map on U is represented appropriately. IsManifold is a chart/groupoid predicate and is not itself the quoted regular-level-set characterization; its more general boundary/corner models must not be imported into this embedded Euclidean definition. A surjective derivative has a kernel of the tangent dimension, and the source normal space is that kernel's Euclidean orthogonal complement, after proving independence of the defining equations. The letter F here is a smooth defining map, distinct from the later set-valued variational map and Theorem 2.7's particular defining map G.

variant_reviews.comparison: The order is exists U around x-bar, then for almost every z, for every x in U, A(.,z) is differentiable at x. It is stronger than a separate exceptional z-set for each x. fderiv supplies the Jacobian only on that differentiability domain; its zero fallback is not evidence of smoothness. MemLp of A(x,.) at exponent two and of its continuous-linear-map derivative at exponent two can express pointwise moment finiteness with appropriate measurability. In addition the expectations of their squared norms must be bounded uniformly in x by finite constants; pointwise MemLp alone does not suffice, and a real sSup default for an unbounded set must not make the displayed finiteness automatic. The Jacobian uses operator norm. This assumption does not give a random Lipschitz bound on the Jacobian, which Theorem 3.1 adds separately, or authorize adding that stronger hypothesis to Theorem 3.2.

variant_reviews.comparison: Definition 2.6 starts at (x-bar,v-bar) on graph F and requires local equality of graph F^-1 with graph sigma near (v-bar,x-bar). For the inclusion 0 in F(x-bar), the intended inverse graph is therefore near (0,x-bar), as explicitly localized in Theorem 3.1. Assumption A nevertheless calls F smoothly invertible at (0,x-bar), reversing the original definition's basepoint order. Function.graph represents the single-valued sigma side, while the inverse relation is {(v,x) | v in F(x)}; ContDiffOn expresses C1 on its input neighborhood. This condition does not assert that F is globally single-valued or globally invertible. The ordinary inverse-function theorem for a map with an invertible full derivative is a stronger special-case construction, not a replacement for this set-valued graph hypothesis.

variant_reviews.comparison: J1 requires the full G map measurable. J2 bounds alpha_k above and below by positive constants times k^-gamma for positive indices, with gamma in (1/2,1]; it is not only an eventual upper rate or equality to one specific schedule, and k=0 needs separate initialization rather than division by zero. The history F_k contains x_j for j<=k and noise nu_j only for j<k. Thus nu_k is a difference with zero conditional mean before its new noise is revealed, not a process that should itself be called an F_k-adapted martingale. Require the strict conditional fourth-moment bound E[||nu_k||^4|F_k]<q(x_k), with q bounded on bounded sets, not necessarily globally bounded. Real condExp needs its integrability hypotheses or a justified localization/extended-moment treatment; its nonintegrable zero fallback cannot verify this bound. A conditional bound by random q(x_k) does not automatically imply a uniform unconditional fourth moment. J4 requires x_k in dom F for k>=1. Theorem 5.1 separately narrows gamma to (1/2,1) and assumes convergence, so those facts are not consequences of this standing definition.

variant_reviews.comparison: The derivative is dP'/dP and the outer measure is baseline P, so use P'.rnDeriv P, not the reverse. RN derivatives are extended nonnegative functions describing an absolutely continuous part; representing all of P' requires P' absolutely continuous with respect to P. Converting to a real ratio needs its almost-everywhere finiteness, while evaluating phi on (0,infinity) additionally requires positivity or a separately specified boundary extension. Absolute continuity alone permits zero density, and no singular contribution or zero-density convention is printed. ConvexOn and ContDiffOn at order three describe phi on the positive ray with phi(1)=0. Do not add phi'(1)=0, phi''(1)>0 or a fixed normalization; even a degenerate generator is allowed by the stated class. The real integral's nonintegrable zero fallback is not a divergence value. A specialized KL definition with its own extensions is not an exact replacement.

IsBrownianReal supplies the Brownian law and almost-sure path continuity, while IsGaussianProcess would still need the fractional covariance and continuous version to describe W^H; their independence is a process-level requirement. No verified specialized Ito or fractional Brownian interface was found in the inspected directories. Retain H in (0,1), eta>0 and the source normalization sigma0 squared=1. variant_reviews.comparison: For b>=1, s>=1 and r_i in {1,...,2S} with sum r_i=b, the b=1 branch necessarily has one degree-one entry and integrates uncentered W_u^H over the dyadic cell, multiplying by 2^(j+p). An affine change of variable gives the printed integral on [0,1], still of uncentered W. For b>=2, each factor integrates a power of W_u^H minus the value at the common left cell endpoint and multiplies by 2^(j+p)/r_i factorial. Their product equals the s-variable unit-cube integral of the product divided by product_i r_i factorial, using the product measure identity after interval rescaling. All factors depend on the same random path; the product integration formula is not an assertion that these random factors are independent. Almost-sure continuous paths give finite time integrals of these powers on compact cells. Preserve the range through 2S here even though a later overlined summation restricts entries through S. The shorthand mathfrak W_(p,l) fixes j=0 and k=0, and this time-integral object is distinct from W^H itself and the stochastic price integral.

variant_reviews.comparison: For y in M^tau, A7 defines tangent and normal spaces at pr_M(y), an orthonormal coordinate matrix O_y, and Sigma(y)=O_y transpose Delta_(sigma,delta)^2 O_y. Delta contains tangent standard deviations sigma^alpha0 and normal standard deviations delta*sigma^alpha_perp; these must be squared in the covariance and positive when using the nonsingular Gaussian density. Basis independence relies on equal scaling within each subspace, not on choosing one global frame. The operator integrates phi_(Sigma(y))(x-y)*f(y) with respect to ambient Lebesgue measure restricted to M^tau. Covariance depends on y rather than x and generally changes with location, so this is not convolution with one fixed Gaussian. The source permits arbitrary real f; it does not assert that K_Sigma f is a probability density, and nonintegrable input cannot be handled by treating the library integral's zero fallback as a valid analytic value. The use of pr_M and the tau-offset requires the retained reach/boundary conventions; no appendix construction or zero-scale extension is inserted.

variant_reviews.comparison: Take ambient Lebesgue measure on R^D times a Haar measure on the real orthogonal group O(D), then apply withDensity to the nonnegative joint density h(mu,O). The inspected Haar constructor normalizes on a chosen positive compact set; on the compact group one can normalize the whole group, with any fixed alternative scaling absorbed consistently into h. Require h to integrate to one when H is used as a probability base; the inequalities alone do not assert normalization. The lower bound is a positive constant multiple of exp(-c1||mu||^b1), and the upper bound is a constant multiple of (1+||mu||)^-b2, uniformly for every location and orientation, with c1,b1>0 and b2>2D-1. A product reference measure does not imply the density factors or that location and orientation are independent. This condition applies to H in partial mixtures and H1 in hybrid mixtures; the independent-sampling example is not a universal assumption.

variant_reviews.comparison: First draw the finite count K from pi_K; conditionally on that count draw a K-vector of weights with all Dirichlet concentration entries equal to the positive alpha_K, and draw K iid atoms from H. A dependent or disjoint-union sample space must retain the K-dependent vector length; Kernel and compProd can encode the conditional hierarchy once that Dirichlet kernel is defined and measurable. The finite measure sum then gives P=sum p_k delta_theta_k, with unit mass coming from simplex-valued weights. The source's natural-number convention must give a positive component count for this simplex construction; no zero-component probability law is invented. The saved count-tail condition (9) is an additional assumption in MFM theorem branches, with pi_K/Pi_K the source aliases, and is not imposed on Dirichlet-process alternatives. This is a prior mixing over finite mixture sizes, not a fixed-K model or the infinite stick-breaking DP prior.

variant_reviews.comparison: Q2 is a random probability measure on the D eigenvalue coordinates, drawn once from the supplied tilde-Pi_Lambda law. Conditional on Q2, the mixing measure P uses the base H0=H1 on location/orientation product Q2 on eigenvalues and follows either a DP prior or an MFM prior. Measure.prod implements this conditional base and compProd can retain the joint law of Q2 and P once the selected prior kernel is constructed. Sharing a random base measure is not the same as drawing one eigenvalue vector and forcing it on every component: atoms can draw distinct eigenvalue vectors from the same Q2. Integrating out the shared Q2 can create dependence among component eigenvalues, so unconditional independent draws from a deterministic base cannot replace the hierarchy. The two prior families are alternatives, and the positive covariance domains and full product parameter space from (7) remain required.

variant_reviews.comparison: For every b>0 there exist B0,c2>0 such that for positive small x1,x2 with x1^2<=x2, the outer prior probability that Q2 assigns at least x1^B0 mass to [x1,x1(1+x1^b)]^d times [x2,x2(1+x1^b)]^(D-d) is bounded below by a positive constant multiple of exp(-c2*x1^(-d/2)). Both blocks use relative width x1^b, not x2^b in the second block, and x1^2<=x2 does not imply x1<=x2. This is a probability of a random-measure mass event, not the expected mass itself. The two additional conditions are expectations under the Q2 prior of Q2(min_i lambda_i<=x) for small x and Q2(max_i lambda_i>x) for large x, bounded by exp(-c3*x^(-b3)) and exp(-c4*x^b4) up to constants. Preserve the nonstrict lower-tail event and exponential upper tail, unlike the partial branch's strict lower event and polynomial upper tail. Finite extrema require D>0, and measure-evaluation measurability is needed to define the outer probability and expectations. H1 separately satisfies (10); the lowercase lambda prior alias does not define a second prior.

variant_reviews.comparison: P is a discrete probability on R^D times O(D), with finite or countably many location-orientation atoms. Fix one common positive diagonal Lambda and use covariance O_k transpose Lambda O_k for component k. Thus eigenvalues are shared but orientations and locations vary, and the covariance matrices need not all be equal. Measure.sum constructs the atom law and measurable binding constructs its Gaussian mixture; density identification and normalization remain to be proved. The displayed integral label R^D omits the orientation variable explicitly carried by dP(mu,O), an inherited notation issue. P follows either a DP prior or an MFM prior; dependency reach to both definitions is not a conjunction. This partial hierarchy differs from the hybrid random-Q2 hierarchy, which shares a law of eigenvalues rather than one eigenvalue vector.

Preserve [n(n-1)]^-1 sum (A_ij-M)^2 = [n(n-1)]^-1 sum A_ij^2-M^2, where square is matrix multiplication. variant_reviews.comparison: Keep P0 fixed; for each P1 in P take an infimum jointly over the estimator and Q in the channel class of the maximum of the two risks at P0,P1, then take the outer supremum over P1. This permits the chosen procedure to depend on the two-point problem and is not inf-over-procedures followed by sup-over-all-P. The observed law Q composed with P is the marginal private sequence generated from iid raw X_i and history-dependent Q kernels, not automatically a product of one-observation output laws. avgRisk at a Dirac prior can express one fixed-P risk after constructing that experiment, but a prior average is not the displayed maximum. Nonnegative extended integrals avoid treating infinite loss expectations as the Bochner integral's default zero; empty estimator/channel classes and finite-real extrema need their own conventions.

variant_reviews.comparison: For finite alpha>1 preserve (alpha-1)^-1 log integral (dP/dQ)^alpha dQ, with the RN derivative an ENNReal function and meaningful handling of an infinite integral. variant_reviews.comparison: Sum over n observed pairs, preserving repeated observations, then multiply by 1/n with n positive. Covariance uses Phi_xi in both slots and maps f to n^-1 sum f(x_i)Phi_xi; cross-covariance uses successor in the second slot and maps f to n^-1 sum f(x_i')Phi_xi. Neither is centered, the denominator is n rather than n-1, and cross-covariance need not be self-adjoint or positive. This construction does not prove existence of the later nonsymmetric empirical fixed point.

variant_reviews.comparison: Under H0 use iid standard Gaussian vectors of dimension 1+p^d. Under H1 a single random vector with independent signs scaled by p^-1/2 generates X-star=sqrt(1-sigma^2) times its d-fold tensor power, shared by all samples; conditional iid sampling does not imply unconditional iid pairs. GaussianReal permits sigma^2=0 as a Dirac noise law. The preceding ||X-star||_F+sigma^2=1 disagrees with the tensor-power formula except special values; preserve both, and do not add unprinted mutual independence between signal, design and errors. Design entries here have variance 1, not the 1/n scaling of other theorem models.

variant_reviews.comparison: Each update samples only coordinate i conditional on all other current coordinates, retaining them unchanged; a deterministic insertion map can lift the conditional kernel. For state-law row action P1...PK updates 1 then 2 through K, whereas Kernel.comp takes the right kernel first, so translate composition order carefully. condDistrib requires a nonempty standard-Borel output and finite law, stronger structure than the unspecified general spaces in this passage. Preserve the printed i=1,...,n discrepancy with K and account for conditional versions on null complements.

The two-block variant first draws the whole local theta block conditional on old psi and data, then draws new psi conditional on the newly sampled theta block and data. compProd retains the first draw while obtaining the second; independent local conditionals given psi/data implement the exact joint block. Reversing order, using old theta in the second draw or replacing exact updates with Metropolis steps changes the kernel. State dimension grows with J and Euclidean conditionals are better specified than the general-space variant.

variant_reviews.comparison: Omega is deterministic and strictly positive definite, chosen outside expectation over xi. Preserve K_e half powers on both sides of (Omega^-1+T-transpose Sigma_w^-1 T)^-1 and the K_c inverse-half trace budget <=varrho^2; powers are spectral, not entrywise, and matrices need not commute. Sigma_w is not explicitly invertible in N2, so do not insert a pseudoinverse or rely on Lean's total inverse. At varrho=0 no positive Omega is feasible, and an empty real supremum default is not specified. Attainment is not guaranteed; expected inverse cannot be replaced by inverse of expected information, and no second moment of T is assumed. Under valid SPD noise the inverse is bounded by Omega, giving a route to integrability despite heavy-tailed T.

variant_reviews.comparison: Take the supremum of Lp norms of inner(X,v) over v^T Sigma v=1, not the Euclidean unit sphere; finite p>=4 and E||X||^p<infinity ensure directional integrability.
